strategies.name: Ratio froth
strategies.tagline: Hold QQQ instead of TQQQ when the TQQQ/QQQ ratio sits more than 19.7% above its own 200-day mean (log extension > 0.18).
strategies.summary: The strategy is the round-1 winner (QQQ above its 165-day SMA -> TQQQ, else BIL, with an armed 4% intraday stop) plus one daily overlay on the TQQQ/QQQ ratio. The ratio's log, 2*log(QQQ) minus 3x realised variance, measures how far leveraged exposure has compounded relative to the drag it paid. When the prior close's log extension above the ratio's 200-day MA exceeds 0.18 - a low-volatility, strongly trending melt-up - the strategy holds QQQ instead of TQQQ for the next session, including overnight. Otherwise it runs the winner unchanged.
strategies.decision: All signals are daily and use only the prior session's close. Before the open of session t: (1) risk-on if QQQ close(t-1) > 165-day SMA of QQQ; (2) ext = log(ratio(t-1) / 200-day MA of ratio(t-1)), ratio = TQQQ/QQQ; (3) if risk-on and ext > 0.18, target 100% QQQ for session t, else if risk-on target 100% TQQQ, else 100% BIL. The target is applied from the 09:31 bar, so the harness fills at the 09:31 open. Separately, on risk-on sessions the 4% stop is armed only when QQQ's first-minute close < prior 20-day SMA * 1.01; if armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, the target becomes BIL at the next minute's open and stays BIL for the rest of the session and the night. There is no intraday signal in the headline version.
rules: Base regime: if QQQ's prior close > its 165-day SMA, risk-on; otherwise hold 100% BIL.

Base stop: on risk-on sessions, arm a 4% stop from the session open only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA * 1.01. If armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the open, sell at the next minute's open and hold BIL for the rest of the session and the night.
Ratio: ratio = TQQQ close / QQQ close; ext = log(ratio / 200-day moving average of the ratio), evaluated at the prior session's close.

Overlay: if risk-on and prior ext > 0.18 (ratio >= 19.7% above its 200-day mean), hold 100% QQQ instead of TQQQ for the next session, including overnight. The 4% stop stays active and takes the book to BIL if it triggers.
Otherwise run the winner unchanged. Long-only, one position at a time, no leverage beyond 100%.
strategies.verdict: Current round-2 leader by 5-year return and rolling consistency: 69.50% / 39.11% (10y) and 63.74% / 26.85% (5y) at 1 bp; strict dominance of the round-1 winner at 1 bp and 5 bp on both windows. It is a fat-tail crash hedge, not stable daily alpha: the overlay fires on 21.5% of sessions, the hit-rate edge is only 2.6 pp, and the 10-year CAGR lead comes from avoiding a handful of melt-up crashes. At 10 bp the 10-year drawdown is 0.47 pp worse than the winner (45.03% vs 44.56%) while CAGR is 6.7 pp higher.

provenance.idea: The TQQQ/QQQ ratio is a decay meter: log(L/L0) = b*log(S/S0) + (b-b^2)/2 * V, so for b=3 the log ratio is 2*log(S/S0) - 3V. This is the reason a high ratio extension means low realised variance, not just a strong QQQ trend.
provenance.source: Avellaneda & Zhang (2010) / Path-Dependence of Leveraged ETF Returns
provenance.evidence: The paper gives the exact formula linking a leveraged fund's price to the underlying and its realised variance, and tests it on 56 double- and triple-leveraged funds. The b=3 special case is the identity used to justify the ratio-extension signal.

provenance.idea: The drag term in the ratio is large and state-dependent: TQQQ's realised financing + fee gap is ~7.2%/yr on top of the path effect, and the volatility break-even for 3x funds is near 14% realised vol.
provenance.source: Adjusted Close / Leveraged ETF "Decay" Is Not What You Think It Is
provenance.evidence: Regresses daily leveraged returns on daily underlying returns (TQQQ/QQQ realised beta 2.957), reports drag ~= 0.5*L*(L-1)*sigma^2 (3*sigma^2 for 3x) and a volatility-quintile table showing leverage beats the naive multiple below ~14% realised vol and loses 19-52 points above it. The 7.23%/yr TQQQ cost gap is the source of the 7.2%/yr figure.

provenance.idea: Low-volatility, strongly trending markets are when leverage and crowding build up, so an extended ratio should raise crash risk rather than lower it.
provenance.source: Brunnermeier & Sannikov (2014) / A Macroeconomic Model with a Financial Sector
provenance.evidence: The 'volatility paradox': low exogenous risk leads intermediaries to choose higher leverage, which makes the system more prone to volatility spikes. This is the mechanism behind treating a high ratio extension as froth rather than momentum.

provenance.idea: Low measured volatility can itself be a catalyst for high future volatility, so a calm melt-up is a risk signal.
provenance.source: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics (2017) / The Low Volatility Puzzle: Are Investors Complacent?
provenance.evidence: States that in Brunnermeier-Sannikov and Adrian-Shin, lower volatility relaxes VaR/margin constraints, leverage rises, and small shocks can force sales and a volatility spike: 'low volatility in itself can be a catalyst for high future volatility.'

provenance.idea: The base 165-day QQQ regime and the general idea of holding a leveraged ETF only above a long moving average.
provenance.source: FinLab (2026) / TQQQ 200-Day Moving Average Strategy: 7 Leveraged ETF Rules
provenance.evidence: 2017-2026 backtest: the QQQ 200-day rule on TQQQ made 45.1% CAGR with a -60.9% max drawdown versus 39.6% / -81.7% buy-and-hold. Also documents the whipsaw cost: 6 of 8 exits saw TQQQ rise while out, which motivated keeping the fast overlay rare.

provenance.idea: The 200-day rule's drawdown reduction and its failure modes on fast crashes.
provenance.source: Exent (2026) / TQQQ and the 200-Day Moving Average: An Exit Rule, Tested
provenance.evidence: Jan 2017 - Sep 2026: 46.4% CAGR / -54.8% max DD with the 200-day rule versus 42.5% / -81.6% held; 34 switches. The worst rule drawdown was the COVID crash, which is why the round-1 base adds a minute stop.

provenance.idea: LETF expected returns are state-dependent, not a constant decay fee, so a variance-adjusted ratio level is the right object to condition on.
provenance.source: Trainor (2025) / Beyond Volatility Decay: Correcting Relative Expected Return Estimates for Leveraged ETFs
provenance.evidence: Shows the standard provider formula misstates long-run LETF expected returns by large amounts depending on the return/volatility state, and that daily LETFs do relatively better in high-return/low-volatility environments.

provenance.idea: Daily re-leveraging and path dependence make a long-horizon LETF/underlying ratio sensitive to realised variance.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
provenance.evidence: Documents that daily re-leveraging creates a path-dependent embedded option and that value can be destroyed for buy-and-hold investors. I used the ResearchGate copy; the web page's SSRN 1393995 link is a different copy that I did not verify.

provenance.idea: Long/short leveraged ETF pair spreads mean-revert, so the ratio might carry relative-value information.
provenance.source: Hessel, Nam, Wang, Cunyu & Zhang (2017) / Shorting Leveraged ETF Pairs (CXO Advisory summary)

strategies.name: ML risk-off overlay
strategies.tagline: A multi-horizon walk-forward logistic risk-off overlay on the daily QQQ trend.
strategies.summary: Three L2 logistic models predict whether TQQQ beats BIL over the next 5, 10 and 20 trading days from 38 causal features. Each model trains on the prior 750 trading days and is retrained annually with an h+1 purge. The average of their trailing 252-day probability ranks must stay at or above 0.20 for TQQQ; otherwise the book moves to BIL. The 165-day QQQ SMA is the base regime, and all fills are at the next open.
strategies.decision: At the close of day i, compute the 38 features from data through that close. Three L2 logistic models (5/10/20-day labels, each trained on the prior 750 trading days and retrained annually with an h+1 purge) output P(TQQQ beats BIL over the horizon). Convert each probability to a trailing 252-day percentile and average the three. Target TQQQ only if QQQ close > its 165-day SMA and the average rank is at least 0.20; otherwise target BIL. The target fills at the next day's open with a 2% band.
rules: Base regime: QQQ close > 165-day SMA means default TQQQ; otherwise BIL.

Three L2 logistic models predict TQQQ-vs-BIL over 5/10/20 trading days from 38 causal features, trained on the prior 750 trading days and retrained each calendar year with the last h+1 boundary rows purged.
Rank each model's probability in its trailing 252-day distribution and average the three ranks.
Target TQQQ only if QQQ close > 165-day SMA AND the average rank is at least 0.20; otherwise target BIL.
Fill at the next day's open with a 2% band; long-only, weights sum to at most 1, no margin or shorting.
strategies.verdict: Passes both windows at 1 bp and 5 bp, with the highest 10y headline (74.95%/40.48%; 5 bp 72.44%/41.09%) and a 5y pass (51.29%/33.20%; 5 bp 48.97%/33.41%). Caveat: this is a daily-decision overlay, not a 30/60-minute strategy. The 30-minute model failed; the 60-minute model only passed at 1 bp (41.87% vs 39.28% 10y, 71.8% DD) and failed at 5 bp (36.32% CAGR, 73.1% DD). The 10y CAGR is 2020-inflated (2020 +403.8% vs TQQQ +99.8%; ex-2020 54.30%); the 48-config grid median is 57.8%/47.1% (10y) and 40.5%/35.6% (5y).

strategies.name: Overnight + first-hour TQQQ with vol filter
strategies.tagline: TQQQ from the close through the first hour, plus a conditional afternoon, behind a 165-day regime, a 20-day volatility filter and a 4% stop.
strategies.summary: A 165-day QQQ regime (2% hysteresis band) switches between TQQQ and BIL. On risk-on days the strategy buys TQQQ at the 15:59 open and holds it through the next session's first hour; the afternoon is held only when QQQ's first-hour return is at least -0.5%. A 20-day realised-volatility filter skips the overnight entry when QQQ vol exceeds 35% annualised, and a 4% stop from the session open exits intraday crashes. 905 fills over 10 years (about 91 per year), long-only, 100% TQQQ or 100% BIL.
strategies.decision: The regime and the 20-day volatility are computed from QQQ daily closes through day d-1, so the state for day d is known before the open. The overnight entry is decided on the 15:58 bar and filled at the 15:59 open. The first-hour return (QQQ 10:29 close divided by the 09:30 open) is evaluated at the 10:29 close and the afternoon position is filled at the 10:30 open. The stop compares the current one-minute TQQQ close with the session open and fills at the next minute's open. All weights are set at bar i and executed at the open of bar i+1; nothing uses data after the decision bar.
rules: Regime (daily, 2% band): QQQ close above 165-day SMA x 1.02 -> ON; below x 0.98 -> OFF; otherwise hold the previous state. The signal uses the close of day d-1 for day d.
Crash filter: skip the overnight entry when QQQ's 20-day realised volatility of daily log returns (annualised, through the prior close) is above 35%.
Overnight plus first hour: when the regime is ON and the vol filter has not fired, buy TQQQ at the 15:59 open (decision bar 15:58) and hold to the next session's 10:30 open.
Afternoon: at the 10:29 close, if the regime is ON and QQQ's first-hour return is at least -0.5%, hold TQQQ from the 10:30 open to the 15:59 open; otherwise hold cash.

Stop: while long TQQQ, if the price trades 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open. A morning stop-out can re-enter at 10:30 only if the first-hour signal is on; an afternoon stop-out stays out for the rest of the session.
Risk-off: 100% BIL whenever the regime is OFF, including overnight.
Execution and costs: next-bar-open fills, long-only, no leverage beyond TQQQ, weights sum to at most 1; 1 bp primary, 5 bp and 10 bp reported.
strategies.verdict: Beats the round-1 winner on the 10-year window at 1, 5 and 10 bp (67.47/36.52 vs 58.80/44.56 at 1 bp; 54.12/41.25 vs 49.50/50.06 at 10 bp) and is materially more consistent across 27 rolling 3-year windows (26/27 beat TQQQ vs 24/27; min 3y CAGR 41.7% vs 31.2%). It is not a strict-dominance winner: its 5-year max drawdown is 2.2-2.4 pp higher than the winner's (35.92% vs 33.49% on minute marks) because of the August 2024 overnight gap. Main caveats: the vol filter only fires in 2020 (23 nights, all March-October) and is inert from 2021 on, and the -0.5% afternoon threshold is fitted.

provenance.idea: The US equity premium is earned overnight (close-to-open), not intraday; this is why the strategy holds TQQQ overnight.
provenance.source: Cliff, M., Cooper, M., & Gulen, H. (2008) / Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours: Like Night and Day
provenance.evidence: Decomposes the US equity premium into open-to-close and close-to-open for stocks, indices and index futures; finds night returns strongly positive and day returns close to zero. Direct license for an overnight TQQQ leg.

provenance.idea: Overnight and intraday blocks are separate clienteles, and momentum-type premia accrue overnight.
provenance.source: Lou, D., Polk, C., & Skouras, S. (2019) / A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns (JFE 134(1), 192-213)
provenance.evidence: Models overnight and intraday returns as driven by different investor clienteles and documents that momentum earn its premium overnight; used to justify keeping the overnight leg and only conditionally trading the session.

provenance.idea: The overnight drift is a large, persistent, cross-asset anomaly rather than a small-sample curiosity.
provenance.source: Haghani, V., Ragulin, V., & Dewey, R. (2022) / Night Moves: Is the Overnight Drift the Grandmother of All Market Anomalies? (JOIM 22(2), 2024)
provenance.evidence: Surveys the overnight-drift literature and documents the effect across indices, ETFs, individual stocks and crypto; supports treating the overnight block as a persistent source of return. No parameter was taken from this paper.

provenance.idea: Close-to-open vs open-to-close decomposition of index returns.
provenance.source: Bondarenko, O., & Muravyev, D. (2021) / Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle (NY Fed Staff Report 917)
provenance.evidence: Documents the overnight drift and its timing around the European open. Important nuance: for S&P 500 futures 1983-2020 it reports open-to-close 5.12%/yr vs close-to-open 3.53%/yr, so the overnight dominance is not universal across instruments; the rule relies on the equity/ETF evidence and on the local TQQQ measurement, not on a futures claim.

provenance.idea: Nasdaq-100 constituents earn the majority of their return overnight.
provenance.source: Liquidnet (2021) / Price Discovery and Tactics to Time Trading
provenance.evidence: Tick-data study reporting that about 65% of the total return of Nasdaq-100 listings is earned overnight (and 80% for S&P 500 names, over 100% for Russell 2000). Used only as corroboration for the Nasdaq-100 overnight share.

provenance.idea: A 3x daily-reset ETF inherits an overnight gap at roughly 3x and cannot be hedged intraday.
provenance.source: Cheng, M., & Madhavan, A. (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds (JOIM 7(4))
provenance.evidence: Explains daily re-leveraging, path dependence and end-of-day rebalancing flows in leveraged ETFs; motivates both the size of the overnight gap exposure and the need for an ex-ante filter rather than only an intraday stop.

provenance.idea: TQQQ end-of-day rebalancing flows are large and mechanical.
provenance.source: ETF.com / One Bad Day: A Levered-QQQ ETF Case Study
provenance.evidence: Case study of the 2018 selloff quantifying the dollar rebalancing TQQQ and SQQQ had to do into the close; used as context for why the close/open boundary is special for a 3x fund.

provenance.idea: High QQQ 20-day volatility is where TQQQ's leverage decay concentrates, so extreme vol is the right crash-filter variable.
provenance.source: FinLab / Leveraged ETF Decay: Volatility Drag and Costs in 14 Funds
provenance.evidence: Reports that days opening with QQQ 20-day volatility above 25% were 22.5% of sessions but carried 52.7% of TQQQ's volatility decay. This is the direct motivation for a 20-day-vol filter; the 35% threshold used here is my own choice, not the paper's 25%.

provenance.idea: The first half-hour / first hour of the session carries information that predicts the rest of the day, so a first-hour signal can condition afternoon exposure.
provenance.source: Gao, L., Han, Y., Li, S. Z., & Zhou, G. (2018) / Market Intraday Momentum (JFE 129(2), 394-414)
provenance.evidence: Documents that the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour, especially on volatile and macro-news days. This agent's rule is the round-1 adaptation (first hour -> whole afternoon), not the paper's exact last-half-hour trade.

provenance.idea: Stop-loss rules add value when returns exhibit momentum, and cost little when they do not.
provenance.source: Kaminski, K. M., & Lo, A. W. (2014) / When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses? (Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254)
provenance.evidence: Provides the theoretical condition under which a stop adds value (momentum/regime shifts) and shows the cost is small otherwise. The 4% level itself is inherited from the round-1 winner, not from this paper.

provenance.idea: Overnight gap-downs tend to revert in the first 30 minutes, so exiting after a gap is the wrong response.
provenance.source: Concretum Group / Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for the SPY
provenance.evidence: Reports that overnight gaps typically revert within the first 30 minutes of the session. This is consistent with my own measurement (TQQQ first 60 minutes average +223 bp after a QQQ gap below -2%, t = 3.61) and is the reason the mandate's gap-down exit was rejected.

provenance.idea: 165-day SMA regime with a 2% hysteresis band; the overnight + first-30-minutes block is the return engine and the last 30 minutes are negative.
provenance.source: quant-trader-research round-1 report: time-of-day (internal)
provenance.evidence: Supplied the 2% band on the 165-day SMA and the evidence that TQQQ's close-to-open and 09:30-10:00 blocks carry the drift while 15:30-16:00 is negative. Its V1 (overnight only) and V2 (overnight + first 30m) are the direct ancestors of this agent's P1/P2.

provenance.idea: A first-hour signal can condition the afternoon; 60-minute formation window; zero threshold as the ex-ante choice.
provenance.source: quant-trader-research round-1 report: intraday-momentum (internal)
provenance.evidence: Its E2 strategy (regime + overnight + first-60m signal -> afternoon) is the base of the recommended strategy here. This agent adds the 20-day vol filter and the 4% stop and changes the threshold to -0.5%.

provenance.idea: Benchmark to beat and the source of the 4% stop level and the 20-day MA arming idea.
provenance.source: quant-trader-research round-1 report: daily-regime-minute-entry (internal)
provenance.evidence: The round-1 winner (165-day regime + armed 4% minute stop) is the comparison target throughout; its 58.80/44.56 and 49.88/33.49 at 1 bp were reproduced exactly. The 4% stop level and the session-open reference are inherited from it.

corrections: Current page (web/public/data/research/strategies.json, slug overnight-crash-filter): the status Verified is correct as a reproducibility label (the simulator matches bt.simulate exactly, the round-1 winner reproduces at 58.80/44.56 and 49.88/33.49, and a truncation test leaves the weight path bit-identical). Verified does not mean leader: keep the 5-year drawdown caveat in the verdict.

Tagline 'Overnight + first hour, with a 35% vol crash filter' oversells the filter and hides half the strategy. The filter skips only 23 nights, all between March and October 2020, and never fires from 2021 to 2026; without it the 10-year max drawdown is 47.85% instead of 36.52%. Better: 'TQQQ from the close through the first hour, plus a conditional afternoon, with a 20-day vol filter and a 4% stop.'

Summary 'Hold TQQQ from 15:59 to 10:30 while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA' is imprecise in two ways: the regime is a 2% hysteresis band around the 165-day SMA (ON above SMA x 1.02, OFF below x 0.98, otherwise unchanged), and the 15:59-10:30 block is only the first of two blocks - the session from 10:30 to 15:59 is held only when QQQ's first-hour return is at least -0.5%.

Metrics on the page show only 1 bp. The 5 bp and 10 bp results were measured and should be shown: 61.40/38.67 and 54.12/41.25 (10y), 46.69/36.32 and 40.83/36.83 (5y). The strategy is unusually cost-robust (905 fills over 10 years, about 91 a year), and the 10-year advantage over the round-1 winner is largest at 10 bp, so omitting those rows understates the result.

Verdict 'Strong 10y; the 5y drawdown is 2.4 pp worse than the round-1 winner' is numerically correct but one-sided. Add that the 5-year CAGR is higher at 1 and 5 bp (51.55 vs 49.88 and 46.69 vs 45.89), that the 10-year result dominates the winner at 1, 5 and 10 bp, and that rolling 3-year consistency is better (26/27 vs 24/27 windows beat TQQQ; min 3y CAGR 41.7% vs 31.2%; max 3y DD 35.4% vs 41.6%).

State the drawdown convention wherever the 5-year number appears: 35.92% is on 1-minute marks while the daily-close drawdown is 31.28% (the round-1 winner is 33.49% minute / 33.08% daily). Mixing conventions would make the comparison wrong in either direction.

Page papers list has three junk entries: a second 'pdf' duplicating Lou-Polk-Skouras, an 'SSRN 4139328' duplicating the Haghani-Ragulin-Dewey entry, and a second 'pdf' for Liquidnet. Deduplicate and label them. The list is also missing Kaminski & Lo (2014, 'When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses?', https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finmar.2013.07.001), which is the source for the stop-loss logic (the 4% level itself comes from the round-1 winner).

Parameter provenance is missing from the page: SMA 165, the 2% band, the 60-minute morning block and the 4% stop are inherited from round 1. The -0.5% afternoon threshold and the 35% vol threshold were chosen on the full sample and are the main overfitting risk; they should not be presented as literature values.

Disclose the overlap with round 1: this is the round-1 intraday-momentum E2 rule (regime + overnight + first-hour signal -> afternoon) plus a 20-day vol filter, a 4% stop and a -0.5% threshold. E2 alone is 66.59/49.15 (10y) and 34.69/37.69 (5y); the additions are worth -12.6 pp of 10-year drawdown and +16.9 pp of 5-year CAGR. It is a blend, not a new standalone signal.

The page name 'First-hour + crash filter' is acceptable but 'First-hour + vol filter' would be more accurate, since the only crash filter is a 20-day realised-volatility threshold and it is a 2020-specific tail hedge rather than a general crash detector.

strategies.name: Gradual stop re-entry
strategies.tagline: Half-size next-session re-entry after a weak stop-day close, full re-entry with a 2% stop after a recovered close.
strategies.summary: Keeps the round-1 winner's QQQ 165-day SMA regime and armed 4% TQQQ stop, then re-enters the next session at 09:31 instead of always waiting a full day. If the stopped session closed above its stop level, it re-enters 100% with a 2% stop for that session; if the close stayed below the stop level, it re-enters only 50% and holds that half through the session and the following night. A clean session restores 100%/4%, and the 2% regime chains after further stops. Same-day VWAP / 5m EMA / 15m EMA / QQQ-MA20 reclaim re-entry was tested and rejected, and is not used.
strategies.decision: Each session: (1) QQQ prior daily close above its 165-day SMA -> risk-on, hold TQQQ, else BIL. (2) On risk-on days, arm the 4% stop only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA x 1.01. (3) If armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the night. (4) Next session at 09:31: if the stopped session closed above its own stop level, re-enter 100% with a 2% stop for that session; if it closed below, re-enter 50% and hold that half through the session and the following night. (5) The 2% stop is checked from the first minute, so a gap-down first minute cancels the re-entry; the 2% regime chains while stops keep firing. All signals use only bars <= i; targets fill at the next bar's open.
rules: Regime: hold TQQQ while QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA; otherwise hold BIL.
Arm the 4% stop only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA x 1.01.
If armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the night.
Weak-close re-entry: if the stopped session closes below its own stop level, hold 50% TQQQ / 50% BIL for the next session (fill 09:31) and through the following night.
Recovered-close re-entry: if the stopped session closes above its own stop level, re-enter 100% TQQQ at 09:31 with a 2% stop from that session's open.
The 2% stop is checked from the first minute and chains after further stops; a gap-down first minute cancels the re-entry. One clean session restores 100% / 4%.
Long-only, one position at a time, no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ; BIL earns its carry while out.
strategies.verdict: Strict dominance vs the round-1 winner at 1, 5 and 10 bp on both windows: 10y 61.03%/39.92%, 5y 51.57%/29.96% at 1 bp; 57.02%/40.68% and 47.65%/30.38% at 5 bp; 52.15%/43.63% and 42.90%/30.90% at 10 bp. The drawdown cut is the robust part (lower in 19 of 27 rolling 3-year windows and all five sub-periods). The CAGR edge is not statistically strong (monthly bootstrap t = 0.65; 90% CI -2.1 to +5.2 pp) and is concentrated in 2018 and 2026, with 2019 and 2024 giving some back. Same-day VWAP/EMA/MA20 re-entry failed and is not part of the rule.

strategies.name: Armed 4% minute stop
strategies.tagline: QQQ 165-day regime with a selective, armed 4% intraday crash stop (~16 triggers a year).
strategies.summary: Hold 100% TQQQ while QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA, else 100% BIL. On risk-on days, arm a 4% stop from the session open only when QQQ is at or below its 20-day MA (+1%); the first 1-minute close 4% below the open moves the book to BIL for the rest of the session and the night, and the position re-enters at the next session's open if the regime is still on. The stop is a crash hedge, not a continuous trading signal: it fired 153 times in the 10-year test window.
strategies.decision: At each session the prior daily QQQ close vs its 165-day SMA sets the regime (TQQQ if above, BIL if below). On risk-on days the arm flag is fixed at the open from the QQQ 09:30-bar close vs MA20 x 1.01, where MA20 is built from daily closes through the prior session. Every minute the strategy checks whether TQQQ's close is 4% or more below that session's open; the first such close sets the target to BIL, filled at the next minute's open. A stopped session stays in BIL through 15:59 and through the overnight, so the next fill is the following session's 09:31 open, where TQQQ is re-bought if the regime is still risk-on. All signals use only bars at or before i, targets fill at bar i+1's open, long-only, 100% TQQQ or 100% BIL.
rules: Regime: QQQ prior daily close > 165-day SMA of QQQ daily closes -> risk-on (100% TQQQ, including overnight); otherwise 100% BIL.
Arm: on a risk-on day, arm the stop only if QQQ's 09:30-bar close is below its 20-day SMA of daily closes (through the prior session) times 1.01.
Stop: while armed, the first 1-minute TQQQ close that is 4% or more below the session open sells at the next minute's open.
After a stop: stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night; re-enter TQQQ at the next session's 09:31 open if the regime is still risk-on.
Long-only, one position at a time, no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ, no shorts; 1 bp one-way base cost, with 5 bp and 10 bp reported.
strategies.verdict: Round-1 winner and the project's strict two-window baseline: 58.80% / 44.56% (10y) and 49.88% / 33.49% (5y) at 1 bp, beating both TQQQ buy-and-hold and the daily QQQ 165-day baseline; it still passes vs TQQQ at 10 bp (49.50% / 50.06% and 41.05% / 34.93%). Rolling 3-year windows: lower drawdown than TQQQ in 27/27, higher return in 23/27. Main caveat: the return edge is a crash hedge concentrated in 2020 and a handful of gap nights (median stop event is about zero), so 58.8% is not a stable annual expectation; the 10y drawdown is still 44.6%.

provenance.source: Faber (2007) - A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation

provenance.idea: Stop-loss rules can add value when returns exhibit momentum / regime shifts, and cost relatively little otherwise.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014) - When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses? Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254
provenance.evidence: Analytical framework showing 0/1 stop-loss rules always reduce expected return under a random walk but can add value in the presence of momentum; daily index-futures evidence that certain stop policies raise expected return while substantially reducing volatility. This is the theoretical license for a conditional stop, and the reason the stop is armed only in weak short-term trends.

strategies.name: First-hour afternoon filter
strategies.tagline: Overnight drift plus a first-hour gate for the afternoon, under a 165-day QQQ regime.
strategies.summary: Hold TQQQ overnight (15:59 to 09:31) and through the first hour while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA. At 10:29 compute the QQQ first-hour return; hold TQQQ for the afternoon only if it is non-negative, otherwise move to cash at the 10:30 open and re-enter at 15:59. Risk-off days are 100% BIL.
strategies.decision: Each session: (1) the 165-day SMA regime uses QQQ's prior close; risk-off means 100% BIL. (2) On risk-on days, enter TQQQ at the 15:59 open (decision on the 15:58 QQQ close vs the SMA through the prior day) and hold through the next 09:31 open. (3) Hold through the first hour. (4) At the 10:29 close compute r60 = QQQ close(10:29) / QQQ open(09:30) - 1; if r60 >= 0 hold TQQQ to the 15:59 open, else sell at the 10:30 open and hold cash until the 15:59 open, then re-enter for the overnight. All signals use only data through the decision bar; all fills are at the next bar's open.
rules: Regime: QQQ close(t-1) > 165-day SMA of QQQ closes through t-1 -> risk-on; otherwise 100% BIL.
Risk-on: hold TQQQ from the 15:59 open through the next 09:31 open (overnight) and through the first hour.
At 10:29 compute r60 = QQQ close(10:29) / QQQ open(09:30) - 1.
If r60 >= 0, hold TQQQ from the 10:30 open to the 15:59 open; if r60 < 0, sell at the 10:30 open, hold cash until the 15:59 open, then re-enter TQQQ for the overnight.
Long-only, weights <= 100%; 1 bp per side primary, 5 bp sensitivity; 2% band; no look-ahead.
strategies.verdict: Passes vs TQQQ at 1 bp and 5 bp on both windows, and beats the daily baseline on all four metrics at 1 bp (10y 55.63%/44.89%, 5y 46.36%/32.64%). At 5 bp the 10y CAGR is 43.46%, 1.85 pp below the baseline's 1 bp figure and about 0.7 pp below the baseline's own 5 bp figure, so this is not a clean win at realistic costs. The max drawdown is the COVID crash (-44.6%), and the first-hour signal is statistically weak (t ~1.4-2.3).

provenance.idea: The first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return (market intraday momentum).
provenance.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) / Market Intraday Momentum, JFE 129(2)
provenance.evidence: Documents the first-half-hour -> last-half-hour effect in SPY 1993-2013 and ten other ETFs, stronger on volatile, high-volume and macro-news days. We tested the mechanism directly: the last-30-minute version does not replicate in QQQ/TQQQ 2016-2026, but the broader first-hour -> afternoon version does (see rejected_sources for the failed last-30m version).

provenance.idea: Intraday momentum is driven by gamma hedging from option dealers and leveraged ETFs; the rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 minutes.
provenance.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021) / Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum, JFE 142(1)
provenance.evidence: Documents intraday momentum across 60+ futures (1974-2020) and links it to hedging demand from market makers and leveraged ETFs. This is the economic rationale for using the first-hour signal to time the TQQQ afternoon and for expecting the effect to be concentrated around leveraged-ETF rebalancing.

provenance.idea: Strategy premia accrue either overnight or intraday; momentum-type premia are earned overnight.
provenance.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) / A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns, JFE 134(1)
provenance.evidence: Documents the overnight/intraday decomposition and the persistence of overnight premia. Our own QQQ/TQQQ decomposition agrees: TQQQ earns 30.2%/yr overnight vs 5.9%/yr intraday (2016-2026), which is why the strategy keeps the overnight leg and why pure intraday timing fails.

provenance.idea: Daily re-leveraging of 3x ETFs creates path dependence and end-of-day rebalancing flows.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds, JOIM
provenance.evidence: Explains the daily reset/path dependence of TQQQ and the mechanical end-of-day hedging flows. Used to motivate the leveraged-ETF channel and the caveat that TQQQ's realized path and future rebalancing flows may differ from a simple 3x overlay.

provenance.idea: Use a 165-day SMA on QQQ as the risk-on/risk-off gate; use cash (not BIL) for the afternoon exit.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source (project daily baseline)
provenance.evidence: The 165-day SMA is the project's pre-existing daily baseline (README: 45.31%/58.71% 10y, 34.61%/36.86% 5y). We inherited the parameter rather than fitting it. Cash-vs-BIL for the afternoon exit was chosen by direct comparison: cash improved 10y CAGR by 2.9 pp at 1 bp and 13.2 pp at 5 bp.

provenance.idea: Overnight drift: US equity returns are concentrated in the close-to-open period.
provenance.source: Haghani, Ragulin & Dewey / Night Moves: Overnight Drift (Elm Wealth)
provenance.evidence: The current web page lists this as a supporting paper. It documents the overnight drift, consistent with our own decomposition (TQQQ 30.2%/yr overnight vs 5.9%/yr intraday). corrections: Rule text ambiguity: the current page says 'Hold TQQQ from 15:59 to 10:30'. This is only the overnight + first-hour leg. After 10:30 the position is held to 15:59 only if r60 >= 0; if r60 < 0 it is sold at the 10:30 open and re-entered at 15:59. The rule list should say this explicitly.

Drawdown convention: the page's 44.89% (10y) and 32.64% (5y) are minute-mark drawdowns; the daily-close marks are 44.59% and 30.37%. The TQQQ 81.68% benchmark is a daily-close figure, so state the convention or show both for comparability.

Paper list: the page includes Elm Wealth's 'Night Moves: Overnight Drift', which is not cited in the original report. Either keep it explicitly as a supporting reference for the overnight drift (medium confidence) or remove it; do not present it as the source of the rule.

Verdict is one-sided: it says 'Fails the daily baseline at 5 bp on the 10y' but does not say that it beats the daily baseline on all four metrics at 1 bp. Add the 1 bp comparison so the reader sees both sides.

Report wording (also applies to the report, not only the page): the 5 bp comparison quotes the baseline's 1 bp CAGR (45.31%). The fair 5 bp comparison is 43.46% vs about 44.2% (roughly a 0.7 pp gap), so the report should label which cost assumption each number uses.

strategies.name: Ensemble crash vote
strategies.tagline: Trend gate + volatility budget + a same-session crash vote.
strategies.summary: A daily QQQ trend gate and a 20-day realised-volatility budget decide the session default: TQQQ when QQQ is above its 165-day SMA and vol is at most 1/3, otherwise BIL. While in TQQQ, a same-session vote from a 60-minute EMA, 30-minute momentum and RSI(14) can cut exposure to BIL for the rest of the day. The only asset actually held in the primary configuration is TQQQ or BIL; QQQ is the tested de-lever alternative.
strategies.decision: At 09:30 ET the session default comes from the prior completed daily close: QQQ above its 165-day SMA and 20-day annualised realised vol at most 1/3 -> 100% TQQQ; otherwise 100% BIL. While the session default is TQQQ, each minute computes three votes: the 60-minute EMA vote is risk-off when QQQ is below it, the 30-minute momentum vote is risk-off when the 30-minute return is negative, and the RSI(14) vote is risk-on when RSI is below 30 (oversold) and risk-off otherwise. If QQQ is at least 3% below the prior close and the vote sum is at most -2, the target becomes BIL at that bar's close and fills at the next minute's open; it stays BIL for the rest of the session. At 15:59 the next session's open is reset from that day's completed close (SMA and vol). All fills are next-bar open; signals use only data through the current bar. The crash exit does not persist overnight; the next session is governed by the daily layer.
rules: Daily trend gate: prior completed QQQ close above its 165-day SMA -> risk-on; otherwise 100% BIL.
Volatility budget: risk-on and 20-day annualised QQQ realised vol at most 1/3 -> 100% TQQQ; vol above 1/3 -> 100% BIL in the primary BIL configuration.
Intraday trend vote: QQQ below its 60-minute EMA is a risk-off vote; above it is risk-on.
Intraday momentum vote: 30-minute QQQ return below zero is a risk-off vote; at or above zero is risk-on.
Mean-reversion vote: 1-minute RSI(14) below 30 is a risk-on vote (do not sell a panic low); RSI at or above 30 is risk-off.
Crash exit: while in TQQQ, if QQQ is at least 3% below the prior close and the three-vote sum is at most -2, sell to BIL at the next minute's open and stay BIL for the rest of the session.
Next-session reset: at the 15:59 close the next open is set from that day's trend gate and vol budget; re-enter TQQQ only if both allow it.
Execution: long-only, one position at a time, 0/1 weights, next-bar-open fills, 2% rebalance band, 1 bp primary cost and 5 bp sensitivity.
strategies.verdict: Passes vs TQQQ on both windows and at 5 bp: 54.73% / 39.91% (10y) and 40.79% / 34.93% (5y) at 1 bp, with Sharpe 1.19 / 0.99 and 225 / 89 fills. It also beats the daily SMA-165 baseline (+9.42 pp CAGR and -18.80 pp DD over 10y; +6.18 pp and -1.93 pp over 5y on 1-minute marks, -3.62 pp on daily closes). Main caveat: the 5-year drawdown margin over the daily baseline is thin on 1-minute marks, the edge is concentrated in high-volatility crash years, and it is not the leader (ratio-pairs is 69.50% / 39.11% 10y and 63.74% / 26.85% 5y).

provenance.idea: Trend following works at slow horizons; mean reversion works at fast horizons. This motivates a daily trend gate plus an intraday mean-reversion veto rather than intraday trend following.

strategies.name: 3% Intraday Crash Stop (SMA-165 regime)
strategies.tagline: Hold TQQQ while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA; step aside for the rest of any session where QQQ falls 3% intraday, then buy back at the next open.
strategies.summary: A daily QQQ 165-day SMA regime holds 100% TQQQ in uptrends and BIL otherwise, with one intraday overlay: while long TQQQ, a 3% QQQ decline versus the previous daily close at any 5-minute close sends the position to BIL for the rest of the session, and it is bought back at the next 09:30 open if the regime is still on. The only genuine mean-reversion leg is that re-entry: after a capitulation the rest of the trigger session is flat (+0.13%), the overnight gap is negative (-0.69%), and the next session's open-to-close is strongly positive (+1.17%). It passes both windows versus TQQQ with a much smaller drawdown, but the return edge is a crash-tail effect concentrated in a few episodes, not a stable per-trade premium.
strategies.decision: At each session's 15:59 close, QQQ close versus its 165-day SMA sets tomorrow's target (TQQQ if above, BIL if below), executed at the next 09:30 open. During the session the stop is evaluated on every 5-minute QQQ close against the previous daily close; a print at or below -3.0% sets a BIL target filled at the next 5-minute open, and re-entry is blocked until the next session. No signal uses data after the bar that sets it; every fill is the next bar's open with 1 bp slippage (5/10/20 bp reported).
rules: Regime: if QQQ close > 165-day SMA of QQQ closes at the session close, target 100% TQQQ; otherwise 100% BIL. Fill at the next session's 09:30 open.
Crash stop: while long TQQQ, if QQQ / prior daily close - 1 <= -3.0% at any 5-minute close, target 100% BIL, filled at the next 5-minute open. At most one stop per session.
Session block: after a stop, no re-entry for the remainder of that session.
Re-entry: at the next session's 09:30 open if the regime is still on. This is the mean-reversion leg (buy back after capitulation).
No other exits; overnight exposure is held while the regime is on. Long-only, weights in {0, 1}, no leverage beyond TQQQ itself.
strategies.verdict: Passes versus TQQQ on both windows (10y 50.96% / 44.83%, 5y 35.50% / 36.29%, 5-minute marks; daily-marked drawdowns 43.38% / 36.16%) and survives 5/10/20 bp. The drawdown cut is structural and parameter-stable (every stop from 1% to 5% passes), but the CAGR edge is not statistically significant (stop-vs-hold +0.61% per event, t = 0.62; daily-return difference t = 0.56) and the stop-level grid CAGR ranges 45-52%. Treat 50.96% as high-40s to low-50s. The 5-year edge over the daily SMA-165 baseline is inside noise.

The defensible claim is 'passes vs TQQQ on both windows and beats the baseline clearly on 10y; the 5y is a near-tie.'

The phrase 'predicts a weak close' is imprecise. On the 48 stop events the rest of the trigger session is +0.13% on average (flat, 48% win); the negative part is the overnight gap (-0.69%), followed by a positive next session open-to-close (+1.17%). Say 'no intraday recovery, a negative overnight gap, then a positive next session'.

The 5-year TQQQ benchmark appears as 13.47% (README) and 13.88% (this dataset, start alignment) in different places on the page. Pick one and footnote the other so the pass margin is not read as two different numbers.

The sentence 'every RSI / Bollinger / VWAP dip-buy variant loses money after 1 bp' is correct for those families, but do not generalise it to all dip-buying: the morning-capitulation variant (QQQ < -1% from the open before 11:00, exit at the close) makes +4.40%/yr net at 1 bp, just far too little to matter.

strategies.name: Opening-range breakout
strategies.tagline: A 30-minute TQQQ opening range, held overnight while the QQQ 165-day regime is on.
strategies.summary: A 30-minute TQQQ opening-range breakout gated by a QQQ 165-day SMA regime, held overnight while the regime is on. Buy the first 1-minute close above the range high after 10:00, stop at the range low, and stay in TQQQ through the night until the stop or the regime turns off; BIL when flat. The intraday-only version is a negative result: TQQQ's open-to-close drift is only about 6%/yr over 10y, so the overnight hold is what makes the strategy pass.
strategies.decision: Each session: (1) build the TQQQ 30-minute opening range from 09:30-09:59 ET; (2) read the QQQ 165-day SMA regime from the prior session's close; (3) if the regime is on and the book is flat, the first 1-minute close above the range high at/after 10:00 and before 15:00 sets a 100% TQQQ target, filled at the next bar's open; (4) while long, a 1-minute low at/below the entry day's range low sets a 100% BIL target, filled at the next open; (5) the first bar of a session whose prior-close regime is off also exits to BIL; (6) otherwise the TQQQ position is held overnight - there is no end-of-day flattening. Signals use only data through the signal bar; every fill is at the next bar's open.
rules: Opening range: TQQQ 09:30-09:59 ET (30 minutes); or_hi = high and or_lo = low of that window.
Regime: QQQ prior-session close > 165-day SMA of QQQ daily closes. When off: no entries, and any long exits on the first bar of the session.
Entry: first 1-minute close above or_hi at/after 10:00 and before 15:00 ET; target 100% TQQQ; fill next bar open.
Stop: entry day's or_lo; a 1-minute low breach triggers a 100% BIL target, filled next bar open. No target, no trail, no max hold.
Overnight: hold the TQQQ position overnight while the regime is on; no end-of-day flattening. BIL when flat.
Costs: 1 bp per fill (5 bp sensitivity); long-only; weights sum to <= 1.
strategies.verdict: Passes vs TQQQ on both windows at 1 bp and 5 bp: 10y 48.98%/48.55% (Sharpe 1.06), 5y 34.08%/42.17% (Sharpe 0.87); 5 bp 48.20%/48.55% (10y) and 33.43%/42.17% (5y). It matches but does not beat the daily baseline on 5y (34.61%/36.86%) and the 10y result rests on about 33 round trips and a few fat winners; the 165-day regime exits late (2020 DD 48%). The pure intraday ORB fails (best 10.27% 10y CAGR), which is the main honest caveat.

strategies.name: Volatility ladder
strategies.tagline: QQQ 165-day regime plus a 1-minute realized-vol ladder from TQQQ to QQQ.
strategies.summary: A daily QQQ 165-day SMA gate decides whether to be invested at all. When risk-on, the strategy sizes a TQQQ/QQQ sleeve from TQQQ's 20-day annualized 1-minute realized volatility: 100% TQQQ below 65%, a linear shift into QQQ between 65% and 95%, and 100% QQQ above 95%. A mild crash throttle moves 5% of the risky sleeve to BIL when QQQ is at least 6% below its 20-day high and TQQQ 5-day realized vol is at least 55%. Fills are next-day open; 1 bp primary, 5 bp sensitivity.
strategies.decision: At each daily close i, compute (a) QQQ close versus its 165-day SMA, (b) 20-day annualized TQQQ realized volatility from within-day 1-minute returns, (c) 5-day TQQQ realized volatility, and (d) QQQ drawdown from its 20-day high. If QQQ close is at or below the SMA, target 100% BIL. Otherwise set x = clip((v20 - 0.65) / (0.95 - 0.65), 0, 1), target QQQ weight = x and TQQQ weight = 1 - x; if QQQ drawdown is at most -6% and v5 is at least 55%, multiply both risky weights by 0.95 and put the rest in BIL. The target set at close i is filled at the open of day i+1; the 2% trade band suppresses small rebalances. No same-bar fills.
rules: Regime: QQQ close above its 165-day SMA -> risk-on; otherwise 100% BIL.

Ladder: with v20 = 20-day annualized TQQQ 1-minute realized volatility, QQQ weight = clip((v20 - 0.65) / (0.95 - 0.65), 0, 1), TQQQ weight = 1 - QQQ weight. This means 100% TQQQ below 65% vol, 100% QQQ above 95% vol.
Crash throttle: if QQQ is at least 6% below its 20-day high and TQQQ 5-day realized vol is at least 55%, scale the QQQ+TQQQ sleeve by 0.95 (5% to BIL).
Execution: signals use the daily close i and are filled at the open of i+1; long-only, weights sum to at most 1; 2% trade band; 1 bp primary, 5 bp sensitivity.
strategies.verdict: Passes vs TQQQ on both windows with much lower drawdown: 10y 47.53% / 45.32% vs TQQQ 39.28% / 81.68%, and 5y 34.59% / 36.29% vs TQQQ 13.47% / 81.68%. The 10y also beats the daily 165-day baseline (+2.22 pp CAGR, -13.39 pp DD), but the 5y CAGR is a 0.02 pp tie (34.59% vs 34.61%) and the 10y edge is concentrated in 2020. The 5y baseline pass/fail flips with small changes in the cut and ladder range, so treat the baseline comparison as fragile; this is crisis risk reduction, not broad alpha.

strategies.name: 5m Donchian breakout
strategies.tagline: A 55-bar QQQ 5-minute breakout, gated by the daily 165-day SMA regime, held in TQQQ until the regime turns off.
strategies.summary: A minute-timeframe adaptation of the Turtle/Donchian breakout. The 55-bar channel supplies the entry trigger; the daily QQQ > 165-day SMA regime supplies the exit and the bear-market filter. The book is 100% TQQQ while long and 100% BIL otherwise, with next-bar-open fills and 1 bp costs.
strategies.decision: Every 5-minute bar, compute the highest high of the prior 55 bars (current bar excluded). If flat, the regime is on, and QQQ closes above that channel, target 100% TQQQ; the order fills at the next 5-minute open. If long and the daily regime is off, target 100% BIL, also filled at the next open. The 15:55 bar is the last bar of the session; its close is the 16:00 print and its target fills at the next session's 09:30 open. No Donchian exit, ATR stop, time exit, or session exit is used in the primary.
rules: Universe and bars: adjusted QQQ/TQQQ/BIL 1-minute data, regular session only, resampled to 5 minutes (78 bars/day), 500 calendar days of warmup.
Entry channel: upper[i] = max(QQQ high over the 55 bars before i); the current bar is excluded.
Regime: QQQ daily close > its 165-day SMA. At the 15:55 bar use the regime through today; at all other bars use the regime through the prior day.
Entry: if flat and regime on and QQQ 5m close > upper, target 100% TQQQ; fill at the next bar's open.
Exit: if long and regime off, target 100% BIL; fill at the next bar's open. No other exit in the primary.
Costs and constraints: 1 bp per fill (5 bp sensitivity), 2% band, long-only, weights sum to 1; BIL earns the T-bill return when out.
strategies.verdict: Passes vs TQQQ on both windows (10y 46.36%/59.79%, 5y 37.46%/40.82%) and survives 5 bp, but it is not a strict improvement over the daily baseline: it gains about 1-3 pp of CAGR and gives up about 1-4 pp of max drawdown. Classic Donchian exits on minute bars fail; the daily regime exit is the only robust exit tested.

strategies.name: 165-day SMA threshold stop
strategies.tagline: Exit intraday at the exact 165-day SMA threshold; re-enter on a regime cross or a new 10-day TQQQ high.
strategies.summary: Daily regime: hold TQQQ while QQQ's close is above its 165-day SMA, otherwise BIL. The 165-day SMA is converted into an exact threshold T_t = mean of the prior 164 QQQ closes; if QQQ trades at or below 0.995 x T_t intraday, the strategy sells TQQQ at the next minute open. After a stop it waits for a new 10-day TQQQ high, unless the daily regime goes bearish first - a bearish close clears the stop state and the next bullish close re-enters at the next open. In March 2020 it exits on 2020-02-28, is stopped out again at the 2020-03-11 open, and avoids the 2020-03-12 collapse; 10y 43.27% CAGR / 45.23% DD, 5y 29.46% / 42.96%. V4 (55% vol target) is the stronger variant: 10y 43.66% / 43.10%, 5y 34.88% / 36.64%.
strategies.decision: At each 1-minute bar i the strategy sees QQQ and TQQQ closes through i. The daily regime uses the last completed daily close (on the 15:59 bar, that session's close). The threshold uses thr_d = rolling(164).mean().shift(1), so thr_d[d] = mean(closes d-164..d-1) is known before day d opens; the code maps it with same_day, not the old per_bar one-day-stale value. If the regime is bullish and QQQ's minute close is at or below 0.995 x T_t, the target flips to BIL; otherwise it stays TQQQ. After a stop, the target stays BIL until either the daily regime resets (bearish then bullish) or TQQQ prints a new 10-day high while the regime remains bullish. The target set at bar i is filled at bar i+1's open by research/bt.py; there are no same-bar fills. Long-only, TQQQ/BIL, weights sum to 1.
rules: Regime: hold TQQQ while QQQ's last completed daily close is above its 165-day SMA; otherwise hold BIL.
Threshold: T_t = mean(QQQ daily closes t-164..t-1); a close at price p today is above the 165-day SMA if and only if p > T_t.
Intraday stop: while long, if QQQ's 1-minute close is <= 0.995 x T_t, sell TQQQ at the next minute open and move to BIL.

Re-entry after a stop: if the daily regime goes bearish, clear the stop state and re-enter at the next open after a bullish close (baseline behavior); if the regime stays bullish, re-enter only when TQQQ's 1-minute close >= max(prior 10 daily TQQQ closes).
Timing and costs: signals use data through bar i only; fills at bar i+1 open; 2% band; 1 bp primary and 5 bp sensitivity; long-only TQQQ/BIL.
strategies.verdict: V1 passes TQQQ on both windows at 1 bp and 5 bp: 10y 43.27% / 45.23% (5 bp 42.70% / 45.84%), 5y 29.46% / 42.96% (5 bp 28.91% / 43.14%). It does NOT beat the daily baseline's 10y CAGR (43.27% vs 45.31%); it cuts the 10y max DD (45.23% vs 58.71%) but has a worse 5y CAGR and DD than the baseline (29.46% / 42.96% vs 34.61% / 36.86%). The 10y return gain is concentrated in March 2020; 2018 is the worst year (-11.6% vs -4.3% baseline) and 2023/2024 also whipsaw. V4 (55% vol target) dominates V1 on all four headline metrics: 10y 43.66% / 43.10%, 5y 34.88% / 36.64% (5 bp 43.07% / 43.55%, 34.28% / 36.66%). The 10y max DD of 45.23% is the 2018-2019 episode, not COVID (2020 DD was 44.87%).

strategies.name: Dual-speed regime
strategies.tagline: 165-day slow gate plus an armed 60-minute EMA(40) filter and a 4% minute stop.
strategies.summary: Keep the 165-day QQQ slow gate as the default regime and hold TQQQ overnight by default. On sessions where QQQ's first minute is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01, a 60-minute QQQ EMA(40) down-cross exits TQQQ to BIL and an up-cross re-enters; a 4% drop of TQQQ from the session open also exits. The fast filter can leave the position in BIL through the close and overnight if the 14:30-15:29 bar is below its EMA; the next session resets to TQQQ at the open when the slow gate is on.
strategies.decision: Each session: (1) the prior QQQ close vs its 165-day SMA sets the default (TQQQ if above, BIL if below); (2) if the default is TQQQ, the session starts long and the arm is evaluated from QQQ's 09:30 first-minute close vs the prior 20-day SMA times 1.01; (3) when armed, each completed 60-minute QQQ bar is compared with EMA(40) - a fresh down-cross sets BIL and a fresh up-cross sets TQQQ; (4) the 4% stop from the TQQQ session open also sets BIL; (5) a weight set at bar i fills at bar i+1's open, and the 14:30-15:29 bar's state carries through the close, so a weak close can leave the position in BIL overnight.
rules: Slow gate: if QQQ's prior session close is above its 165-day SMA, the session's default is 100% TQQQ; otherwise 100% BIL.
Arming: when the slow gate is on, the fast filter and the 4% stop are active only if QQQ's 09:30 first-minute close is below the prior 20-day SMA times 1.01.
Fast filter: on armed sessions, a completed 60-minute QQQ bar closing below EMA(40) exits TQQQ to BIL at the next minute's open; a bar closing back above EMA(40) re-enters.
Stop: on armed sessions, if TQQQ's minute close is 4% below the session open, exit to BIL at the next minute's open.

Session reset: the session starts long when the slow gate is on, so the fast filter only acts on a fresh 60-minute cross; after a stop, re-entry requires a 60-minute up-cross or the next session's open.
Execution: weights are set from bars at or before i and filled at bar i+1's open; long-only, 100% TQQQ or 100% BIL; 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp reported.
strategies.verdict: Strictly dominates the round-1 winner at 1, 5 and 10 bp (10y 70.11/42.91, 61.44/44.25, 51.23/49.25; 5y 61.78/25.88, 53.93/26.81, 44.65/28.57), but the ratio leader still has a lower 10y drawdown (39.11% vs 42.91%) and a slightly higher 5y CAGR (63.74% vs 61.78%). The extra CAGR is concentrated in 2019/2023/2026, the EMA-40 plateau is spans 35-45, and the 10 bp 10y margin is thin.

provenance.idea: Slow trend/MA gate on a broad equity index cuts drawdown, at the cost of return in long bull markets. The 165-day QQQ length and the TQQQ implementation are ours.
provenance.source: Faber (2007/2013) - A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
provenance.evidence: Buy when monthly price is above its 10-month SMA, sell below; the rule roughly halves drawdown but gives up return in bull markets and pays whipsaws in choppy markets. The report uses it as the slow-gate family, not as a literal 165-day parameter source.

provenance.idea: Apply MA-based risk management to leveraged equity rather than to the unlevered index.
provenance.source: Gayed & Bilello (2016) - Leverage for the Long Run
provenance.evidence: Moving-average risk management applied to leveraged equity; cited by the round-1 winner and by the web page. It supports the slow gate on TQQQ, not the 60-minute filter.

provenance.idea: Faster trend models truncate the left tail but have worse after-cost Sharpe and much higher turnover; this motivated keeping the fast filter armed and intraday-only.
provenance.source: Man Group / Man AHL (2023) - The Need for Speed in Trend-Following Strategies
provenance.evidence: Table 2/3: Sharpe falls from 1.09 for the slow model to 0.69 for the very fast model before costs (0.40 after costs); skewness is positive for fast models. Speed buys crash protection and costs turnover, so the fast leg should be rare and gated.

provenance.idea: Reactive signals capture short-term trends but are prone to whipsawing; less reactive signals are steadier but late.
provenance.source: Graham Capital (2018) - The Speed of Trend-Following
provenance.evidence: Explicit statement of the speed trade-off: reactive signals capture short-term trends but can whipsaw; less reactive models are steadier but late to reversals. This is why the 60-minute filter is only allowed to act when the daily trend is already weak.

provenance.idea: Absolute-momentum/trend filters do the risk work, but a 12-month filter cannot react to a crash inside a month; a second, faster 1-3 month check is the suggested fix; choppy markets cause whipsaw.
provenance.source: AlgoStrategyLab (2026-10-22) - I Backtested Dual Momentum for 29 Years
provenance.evidence: 29-year GEM replication: 10.25% vs 9.85% CAGR, 34% vs 55% max DD; the trend filter does the risk work; the worst drawdown was 2020 because the filter was still positive at the bottom; the article recommends a second faster overlay, accepting more whipsaw. Used as the design brief for a fast leg on top of the slow gate.

provenance.idea: How often a slow average is checked matters: daily checks whipsaw far more than monthly checks, and 78% of daily 200-day switches reverse within a month; bands help.
provenance.source: BestFolio (2026-11-10) - The best trend filter depends on the year you start
provenance.evidence: 49-year SPY/QQQ study: daily 200-day rule 9.60% CAGR vs 10.96% at month-end on SPY; 78% of daily switches reversed within a month; a 3% band restored most of the return. Used to reject a fast daily gate and to keep the fast leg intraday.

provenance.idea: Simple price-vs-MA rules have high false-signal rates (57-76%), so a faster filter must be gated rather than always on.
provenance.source: QuantifiedStrategies (2025-06-02) - How Likely Is a False Signal in Moving Average Trading?
provenance.evidence: S&P 500 1960-2025 test of 5-200 day lookbacks: win rates 24-43%, i.e. 57-76% false signals. Supports the arming condition and the crossover (rather than level) implementation.

provenance.idea: Smoothing the trigger and using a longer fast MA raises the win rate; the 50/200 cross was the best risk-adjusted pair in a standard test.
provenance.source: StockCharts SystemTrader (2016-11) - How to become a Smooth Operator with Moving Averages
provenance.evidence: The 50/200-day SMA cross had the highest risk-adjusted return of the tested pairs, and win rates rose as the fast MA lengthened; daily close-based triggers whipsawed most. Used to justify a smoother fast leg (60-minute bars, EMA-40) rather than a 1-minute signal.

provenance.idea: A 10-month/200-day trend filter cuts drawdown roughly in half but pays about 2.6 pp/yr in a bull market; whipsaws are the main cost.
provenance.source: MarketHeist (2026-10-31) - The 10-month trend filter: how it works, what it costs, whipsaws
provenance.evidence: SPY 1986-2026: 11.0% to 8.5% CAGR, -50.8% to -26.4% DD, 1.5 switches/yr, 22 whipsaw exits. Used as the base-rate cost of trend filters and the reason not to replace the slow gate with a fast one.

provenance.idea: The 10-month rule on QQQ cuts the worst drawdown from -74.6% to -25.4% but gives up 4.3 pp/yr in 2013-2026.
provenance.source: Quantum Bias - Moving Average Strategy Tested: The 10-Month Rule on the Nasdaq
provenance.evidence: QQQ replication: 9.2% buy-and-hold vs 10.9% for the 10-month rule, -74.6% vs -25.4% DD; 2013-2026 gave up 4.3 pp/yr. Same slow-gate trade-off as Faber, on the same instrument family.

provenance.idea: Stop-loss rules add value when returns have momentum/regime shifts; this is the license for keeping the 4% minute stop.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014) - When do stop-loss rules stop losses?
provenance.evidence: Theoretical and empirical condition for stop-losses to add value under momentum/regime shifts. The report keeps the round-1 4% stop because the fast filter alone leaves the 2020 gap crash unprotected (10y DD 55.44% without it).

provenance.idea: Overnight and intraday expected returns differ; TQQQ's drift is concentrated overnight, so a fast gate that holds BIL for whole sessions is expensive.
provenance.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) - A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
provenance.evidence: The paper documents the overnight/intraday return difference. Our own 2017-2026 decomposition (round-1 report) is +1,355% overnight vs +81% intraday for TQQQ; the fast filter is therefore intraday-only and the slow gate owns the default overnight.

provenance.idea: General trend-following/industry-trend premise.
provenance.source: Zarattini & Antonacci (2024) - A Century of Profitable Industry Trends
provenance.evidence: Listed on the current web page. It supports trend following in general but does not contain a 60-minute EMA rule and did not drive this design; the fast/slow speed evidence came from Man AHL, Graham, AlgoStrategyLab and BestFolio.

provenance.idea: The specific 60-minute EMA(40) span, the 165-day length, the 4% stop, the +1% arm, the daily session reset, the crossover-vs-level choice, and the 09:30-aligned 60-minute bar convention.

It is a core component, not an optional extra: without it the 10y drawdown is 55.44%, not 42.91% (the fast filter alone does not protect the 2020 gap crash). strategies.name: OpEx de-risk
strategies.tagline: Overlay on the 165-day winner: keep the overnight TQQQ leg, step aside for the OpEx session only.
strategies.summary: An overlay on the round-1 winner, not a standalone system. The base holds 100% TQQQ while QQQ's prior close is above its 165-day SMA (else BIL) and runs the winner's armed 4% intraday stop. On monthly option-expiry sessions (third Friday, holiday-shifted) the overlay keeps the overnight TQQQ position but holds BIL from the 09:31 open to the 15:59 close, then buys TQQQ back. An optional variant also de-risks scheduled FOMC decision days.
strategies.decision: At the 09:30 bar of session d the strategy already knows the daily regime (QQQ close[d-1] vs its 165-day SMA) and whether d is an OpEx or scheduled-FOMC calendar date; both are ex-ante. If the regime is risk-off the target is BIL. If the regime is risk-on and d is an OpEx session, the 09:30 bar targets BIL so the sell fills at the 09:31 open, and the 15:58 bar targets TQQQ=1 so the buy-back fills at the 15:59 open; the overnight leg is never touched. The winner's 4% stop runs unchanged on top: when armed (QQQ 09:30 < 20-day SMA * 1.01) and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, the target moves to BIL at the next minute's open and stays there for the rest of the day and the night. Every target set at bar i fills at open(i+1); no price after bar i is used.
rules: Base regime: risk_on = QQQ close[d-1] > 165-day SMA of QQQ closes through d-1. Risk-on -> 100% TQQQ (held overnight); risk-off -> 100% BIL.

Base stop: on risk-on sessions, arm only when QQQ's 09:30 print is below its 20-day SMA * 1.01; if armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and hold BIL for the rest of the session and the night.

Overlay (primary, V1): on a monthly option-expiry session (third Friday; rolled back to the prior session when that Friday is an exchange holiday, e.g. 2026-06-19 Juneteenth -> 2026-06-18), keep the overnight TQQQ leg and hold 100% BIL from the 09:31 open to the 15:59 open, then buy TQQQ back.
If the base strategy is already in BIL (risk-off or stopped out), the overlay changes nothing.
Optional leg (V4): apply the same intraday-only de-risk to scheduled FOMC decision days. Reported, not promoted: the FOMC intraday swap gain is +26.3 bp with t = 1.04.
Fills are always the next bar's open; costs are 1 bp one-way in the headline, with 5 bp and 10 bp also reported.
Long-only, weights sum to <= 1, no leverage and no shorts; 1-minute regular-session bars only.
strategies.verdict: Strict 10-year dominance of the round-1 winner at 1/5/10 bp (+8.26/+5.91/+3.17 pp CAGR, -3.92/-4.02/-2.73 pp DD) and better rolling 3-year consistency (beats the winner on both CAGR and DD in 27 of 28 windows), but the 5-year drawdown is 2.39 pp worse at 1 bp (35.88% vs 33.49%), so it fails the 'lower DD on both windows' bar. OpEx was selected after seeing that FOMC, CPI, NFP and pre-holiday de-risking all lose money, so the effect is a research candidate, not a settled anomaly.

strategies.name: ATR-scaled crash stop
strategies.tagline: One-sided volatility scaling: tighten the stop in calm markets, never widen it past the round-1 4%.
strategies.summary: Keeps the round-1 winner exactly - QQQ above its 165-day SMA holds TQQQ, otherwise BIL - but replaces the fixed 4% intraday stop with stop = clip(0.70 x TQQQ daily ATR(14), 2.5%, 4%). The stop is armed only when QQQ's 09:30 close is below MA20 x 1.01; a trigger exits to BIL at the next bar's open for the rest of the session and the night. Net effect: 62.60% / 40.94% (10y) and 54.88% / 33.49% (5y) at 1 bp versus the winner's 58.80% / 44.56% and 49.88% / 33.49%.
strategies.decision: Before each session the daily regime (QQQ prior close vs its 165-day SMA) and the stop distance (TQQQ ATR(14) through the prior close) are already known. The regime sets 100% TQQQ or 100% BIL for the session. On a risk-on session, the stop is live only if QQQ's 09:30 one-minute close is below its 20-day SMA x 1.01. If armed and TQQQ's one-minute close falls below session_open x (1 - stop distance), the target weight flips to 100% BIL on that bar and the harness fills it at the next bar's open. The book stays BIL through 15:59, so it is also out overnight, and re-enters TQQQ at the next session's open if the regime is still on. No same-day re-entry, no shorts, weights sum to 1.
rules: Regime: QQQ prior close > 165-day SMA of QQQ daily closes -> 100% TQQQ, else 100% BIL (signal from the prior close, filled at the next open).
Stop distance: 0.70 x ATR(14) of TQQQ daily bars (aggregated from the adjusted 1-minute panel) through the prior close, floored at 2.5% and capped at 4.0%.
Arm gate: the stop is live only when QQQ's 09:30 one-minute close is below its 20-day SMA x 1.01 (MA through the prior close).
Trigger: on an armed session, exit to 100% BIL when TQQQ's one-minute close falls below session_open x (1 - stop distance).
Execution: the exit target is set on the trigger bar and filled at the next bar's open; the book stays BIL for the rest of the session and the night.
Re-entry: the next session starts 100% TQQQ at the open if the regime is still risk-on, otherwise BIL.
strategies.verdict: Strictly dominates the round-1 winner on the 10y window (62.60% vs 58.80% CAGR, 40.94% vs 44.56% max DD) and adds +5.0 pp of 5y CAGR with an identical 5y max drawdown (33.49%, same 2026-06-22 -> 2026-07-30 peak/trough and the same eight stop days at exactly 4.00%). Passes at 5 bp (57.01% / 44.25% and 49.75% / 34.13%) and at 10 bp (50.29% / 48.12% and 43.57% / 34.93%). Main caveat: the 5y result is a CAGR win plus a drawdown tie, not a 5y drawdown improvement, so the README's literal strict-dominance test is met only on 10y; and the 4% cap is inherited from the round-1 winner rather than discovered out of sample.

provenance.idea: Express the stop as a multiple of ATR rather than a fixed percentage (the Chandelier/ATR-exit construction).
provenance.source: Quant Arenas - Chandelier Exit strategy backtest
provenance.evidence: Standard ATR-multiple exit template (highest high - 3 x ATR). Used for the form of the rule; the multiplier and reference point (session open, not a trailing high) were chosen from own tests.

provenance.idea: ATR-scaled stops are a well-known family, but empirically they are not automatically better than percentage stops.
provenance.source: Volatility Box - Volatility-Adjusted Stop Losses: ATR, Chandelier, and Keltner Methods
provenance.evidence: Compares four volatility-adjusted stop methods; reports the Chandelier variant as best of the four but with only a modest edge. Used as a caution that the ATR form alone is not the edge - which matched the finding that the one-sided cap, not the ATR multiple, is what makes this work.

provenance.idea: The ATR multiplier should be O(1), and a floor is needed because sub-1.0x ATR stops get destroyed by micro-noise.
provenance.source: FXNX - Stop-Loss Distance vs Hit Rate: 20,000-Trade Study
provenance.evidence: 20,000-trade FX study: sub-1.0x ATR stops collapse hit rates by >40%; 1.3-1.8x ATR is the reported sweet spot. Used to sanity-check that a 2-3x ATR stop is not automatically 'wider is safer' and that a 2.5% floor is needed at the tight end.

provenance.idea: Stop-loss rules add value when returns have momentum / negative conditional skew, and always reduce expected return under a random walk.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014) - When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses?
provenance.evidence: The theoretical license for a stop that is armed only in weak short-term trends: the stopping premium is positive under momentum and negative under a random walk, so the level and the arming condition matter. Inherited from the round-1 winner; not re-derived here.

provenance.idea: Volatility-scaled risk exposure is a legitimate family (inverse-variance / volatility-managed portfolios).
provenance.source: Moreira & Muir (2017) - Volatility-Managed Portfolios
provenance.evidence: Managed portfolios that take less risk when volatility is high produce large alphas and higher Sharpe ratios. Used as background for scaling risk with volatility; the symmetric (widen the stop when vol rises) application was tested and rejected in this setting.

provenance.idea: A fixed percentage stop is a different amount of 'normal travel' in calm vs volatile regimes, so the distance should be volatility-dependent.
provenance.source: Arrow Algo - Volatility Clustering: What It Is and How to Trade It
provenance.evidence: A 1% stop may be two hours of normal movement in a calm market and twenty minutes during a volatility cluster; argues for sizing stop distance off recent volatility.

provenance.idea: A large stop-loss study finds ATR-scaled stops roughly match percentage stops and trailing ATR stops underperform.
provenance.source: Cesar Alvarez (Better System Trader #037) - Stop loss types tested
provenance.evidence: Used as the null hypothesis: at 3 ATR the results were nearly identical to a 10% percentage stop, and trailing ATR stops had negative/weak expectancy. This is counter-evidence, not support - the test here had to show something the study says is not automatic, and the difference came from the one-sided 4% cap.

provenance.idea: Partial exits usually reduce returns relative to the better of 'stay in' or 'get out'.
provenance.source: Enlightened Stock Trading - Is Taking Partial Profits in Trend Following a Rational Idea?
provenance.evidence: Systematic tests of partial profit-taking inside trend-following show it reduces overall return. Consistent with the tested-and-rejected 50% QQQ de-risk, which cut CAGR more than drawdown.

provenance.idea: Partial exits are often not the thing that helps; the stop rule is.
provenance.source: TradeJournal - Scaling Out of Trades: Does Taking Partial Profits Help or Hurt?
provenance.evidence: Argues the partial exit is usually not what produces the improvement and should be tested separately from the stop move. Used when interpreting the 50% QQQ de-risk result (return sacrificed, little drawdown benefit).

provenance.idea: 3x daily leverage multiplies both the distance and the volatility drag, so a TQQQ percentage stop is a small index move.
provenance.source: FinLab - Leveraged ETF Decay: Volatility Drag and Costs in 14 Funds
provenance.evidence: TQQQ trailed 3x QQQ by ~22 log points a year over 2016-2026, about 15 from volatility. Used to calibrate that a 2.5-4% TQQQ stop is only ~0.8-1.3% on the index, i.e. a normal intraday move rather than a wide stop.

provenance.idea: The 165-day SMA regime itself (inherited unchanged from the round-1 winner).
provenance.source: Faber (2007) - A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation / Gayed (2016) - Leverage for the Long Run
provenance.evidence: Trend-following risk management with a long moving average applied to a leveraged equity position. The specific 165-day length is the round-1 implementation, not re-optimised here.

provenance.idea: The 4% cap, the 2.5% floor, the 0.70 multiplier, the MA20 arm gate, the next-open fill convention and the rejections (partial de-risk, uncapped ATR, literal 2-3x intraday ATR).
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL data via research/bt.py. The 4% cap is the round-1 winner's stop (own test), the 2.5% floor is a microstructure-noise bound (~16x TQQQ's 1-minute ATR), and the 0.70 multiplier is the centre of the 0.55-0.75 plateau. Partial de-risking and uncapped ATR were tested and rejected on the same data.

rejectedSources.why_rejected: Its concrete prescription - set stops at ~2x the 20-day ATR - was tested and rejected for a session-open stop: 2x daily ATR is ~8.4% and never binds before the regime flips, while 2x ATR on 1m/5m bars is ~0.3%/0.7% and fires on noise. The useful part (stops should scale with the volatility regime) was kept; the 'wider in high vol' direction is wrong for a gap hedge here.

corrections: The page writes 'clip(0.70 x ATR14, 2.5%, 4%)' without a bar size. It must be TQQQ DAILY ATR(14), built from the adjusted 1-minute panel aggregated to daily bars and taken through the prior close. A literal 2x/3x ATR on 1m bars is ~0.3%/0.5% and on 5m bars ~0.7%/1.0% - both are noise-level stops (3xATR5m produced 502 stops and 49.42% CAGR). This is the difference between implementing the strategy and implementing something else.

Add the arm gate and execution to the rules: the stop is armed only when QQQ's 09:30 one-minute close is below its 20-day SMA x 1.01; the exit fills at the next bar's open and the book stays BIL for the rest of the session and the night, re-entering TQQQ at the next open if the regime is still on. The page currently says only 'Base: round-1 winner'.

Paper attribution: STOP_STUDY (Cesar Alvarez) is counter-evidence, not support - that study finds ATR stops roughly match percentage stops and that trailing ATR stops underperform. Listing it alongside ATR and MOREIRA implies it inspired the rule. Either mark it 'tested only' or replace it with Kaminski & Lo (2014), which is the actual theoretical support for an armed stop.

As written it can be read as a 5y drawdown improvement.

Status: 'Alternative' is defensible under the literal criteria (the 5y DD is a tie), but if the site's taxonomy means 'Verified = passes the bar', this entry qualifies - it passes at 1/5/10 bp and strictly dominates on 10y. The label should be applied consistently across round-2 entries.

strategies.name: Winner/ensemble 75/25
strategies.tagline: 75% round-1 winner + 25% round-1 ensemble, combined as one target-weight portfolio.
strategies.summary: Combine the round-1 winner (daily QQQ 165-day SMA regime + armed 4% minute stop) and the round-1 ensemble (trend + 20-day volatility budget + 1-minute crash vote) in one account. At every bar the target weight vector is 0.75 x winner target + 0.25 x ensemble target. Both sleeves hold only TQQQ or BIL, so the portfolio is 100% TQQQ when they agree and a partial TQQQ/BIL mix when they disagree; it is a lower-risk substitute for the winner, not a higher-return one.
strategies.decision: Daily regime signals use the prior 15:59 close (QQQ close vs its 165-day SMA). The winner's stop is armed at the first minute using QQQ's first-minute close vs its prior 20-day SMA x 1.01, and triggers when TQQQ closes 4% below the session open; the fill is the next minute's open. The ensemble's 20-day realised-vol budget uses the prior daily closes, and its crash vote uses the current minute's QQQ return, 60-minute EMA, 30-minute momentum and 1-minute RSI, filling at the next minute's open. At the close of bar i both sleeve target vectors are computed from data through bar i, blended 0.75/0.25 into one target, and filled at bar i+1's open; a 2% band suppresses small rebalances. Positions are held overnight unless a sleeve rule changes.
rules: Winner sleeve: QQQ prior close > 165-day SMA -> 100% TQQQ, else BIL. On risk-on days arm a 4% stop from the session open only when QQQ's first-minute close < prior 20-day SMA x 1.01; if armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the open, sell at the next minute's open and stay BIL for the rest of the session and night.

Ensemble sleeve: QQQ 165-day trend gate; 20-day realised QQQ volatility <= 33.3%, else BIL; a same-session crash vote (QQQ <= -3% from the prior close and trend/momentum/RSI vote <= -2) exits TQQQ to BIL for the rest of the session.
Blend: target = 0.75 x winner target + 0.25 x ensemble target, with columns QQQ/TQQQ/BIL; long-only, weights sum to 1, and any uninvested residual is BIL.
Execution: signal at bar i close, fill at bar i+1 open, 2% rebalance band; no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ and no shorting.
strategies.verdict: Meets round-2 target #2 at 1 bp on both windows (10y -0.38 pp CAGR / -3.38 pp DD; 5y -1.96 pp CAGR / -1.16 pp DD versus the winner) and still meets it at 5 bp and 10 bp. It beats the winner outright on the 10-year window at 5 bp (54.91% vs 54.60%, DD 43.39% vs 47.08%) and 10 bp (50.63% vs 49.50%, DD 46.04% vs 50.06%). It is not strict dominance: the 5-year 1 bp CAGR margin is only 0.04 pp inside the 2 pp rule, and 5-year Sharpe is slightly below the winner (1.126 vs 1.156).

provenance.evidence: Explains the concave payoff of rebalancing two strategies and shows an optimal blend can outperform either; used to justify the fixed-weight curve and the 75/25 choice.

provenance.idea: The mathematical rebalancing/diversification return that makes a fixed-weight mix differ from a buy-and-hold mix.

provenance.idea: Geometric-return (rebalancing-premium) framing of fixed-weight portfolios.
