strategies.name: Dynamic leverage
strategies.tagline: 30% TQQQ core + 70% 65%-vol-target sleeve, with the winner's armed 4% minute stop.
strategies.summary: On risk-on sessions (QQQ prior close above its 165-day SMA), hold a 30% permanent TQQQ core and put the other 70% into an inverse-vol TQQQ sleeve that targets 65% annualised 20-day volatility, with BIL as the residual; on risk-off sessions hold 100% BIL. The round-1 winner's armed 4% minute stop is applied on top. At 1 bp it returns 57.05% / 41.32% over 10 years and 50.12% / 30.16% over 5 years, versus the winner's 58.80% / 44.56% and 49.88% / 33.49%.
strategies.decision: At each session's close, compute QQQ's 165-day SMA and TQQQ's 20-day realised volatility from daily closes; both are known before the next open. If QQQ's prior close is below its 165-day SMA, target 100% BIL. Otherwise target w_TQQQ = 0.30 + 0.70 × min(1, 0.65 / vol20), with BIL for the remainder; the 2% trade band suppresses small daily resizes. These daily targets are set from the prior close and fill at the next bar's open (09:31 for the first bar of the session). Intraday, on a risk-on day, the 4% stop is armed only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA × 1.01; if armed and TQQQ's 1-minute close falls 4% below the session open, the whole book is sold at the next minute's open and held in BIL for the rest of the session and overnight. No same-bar fills.
rules: Regime: if QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA, the next session is risk-on; otherwise hold 100% BIL.

Risk-on sizing: w_TQQQ = 0.30 + 0.70 × min(1, 0.65 / vol20), where vol20 is the annualised 20-day standard deviation of TQQQ daily close-to-close log returns through the prior close; the remainder is BIL.
Long-only, weights sum to at most 1, and TQQQ weight never exceeds 100% (no leverage beyond TQQQ's embedded 3×).
Arm the stop only on a risk-on day when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA × 1.01.

If armed and TQQQ's 1-minute close is 4% below the session open, sell the whole book at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night; re-enter next session if the regime is still on.
Daily targets are set from data through the prior close and fill at the next bar's open; the 2% rebalance band applies.
strategies.verdict: Meets the round-2 'lower drawdown with CAGR within 2 pp' test on both windows and at 1, 5 and 10 bp: 10y 57.05% / 41.32% vs the winner's 58.80% / 44.56% (CAGR −1.75 pp, DD −3.24 pp), 5y 50.12% / 30.16% is strict dominance. Calmar improves from 1.32 to 1.38 (10y) and 1.49 to 1.66 (5y). Main caveat: the 10y pass has only a 0.25 pp cushion (57.05% vs the 56.80% floor; the 20% core neighbour is 56.71% and misses), and rolling return wins are 22/27 vs the winner's 23/27, so the consistency gain is in drawdown, not return. The CAGR give-up is concentrated in the 2020 V-recovery.

provenance.idea: Scale exposure inversely to recent realised variance; volatility-managed equity portfolios raise Sharpe because volatility changes are not matched one-for-one by expected-return changes.
provenance.source: Moreira & Muir (2017) / Volatility-Managed Portfolios
provenance.evidence: The inverse-vol TQQQ sleeve (65% target, 20-day window) is a capped implementation of their volatility-managed portfolio. Their mechanism is the reason the strategy cuts exposure when TQQQ vol is high rather than after a loss.

provenance.idea: Volatility targeting improves Sharpe and reduces the severity of left-tail events and maximum drawdowns; a slow, broad realised-vol estimator is preferred to a fast timing signal.
provenance.source: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison & Van Hemert (2018) / The Impact of Volatility Targeting
provenance.evidence: Supports the 20-day daily-close estimator and the claim that the main benefit is drawdown/tail reduction, not higher average return. The paper also documents the cost of targeting too aggressively, which motivated the 30% permanent core.

provenance.idea: Volatility-managed portfolios often fail out of sample because of estimation instability, so the adjustment should be tempered rather than an all-or-nothing vol switch.
provenance.source: Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan (2020) / On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
provenance.evidence: This is the main reason the implementation keeps a 30% permanent TQQQ core and applies the vol target only to the other 70%. A pure 65% target has the best Calmar but gives up 2.66 pp of 10y CAGR, outside the 2 pp band.

provenance.idea: Conditional volatility targeting can enhance Sharpe and reduce drawdowns and tail risk with low turnover.
provenance.source: Bongaerts, Kang & van Dijk (2020) / Conditional Volatility Targeting
provenance.evidence: Supports a conditional/tempered vol-target rule instead of a constant leverage; the paper's low-turnover finding is consistent with the 2% band and ~93.9% average TQQQ target weight here.

provenance.idea: For excess mean μ and variance σ², the growth-optimal fraction is f* = μ/σ²; full Kelly is too aggressive under parameter uncertainty, so fractional Kelly is the practical choice.
provenance.source: Thorp (2006) / The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market
provenance.evidence: The 30/70 blend is a shrunk inverse-vol rule in the same spirit as fractional Kelly: keep a fixed core, apply a fraction of the vol-target adjustment. The literal daily Kelly formula was tested separately and rejected (see rejected_sources).

provenance.idea: A daily-reset 3× ETF's multi-day log return is approximately 3× the index log return minus 3 × the sum of squared daily returns; volatility drag and path dependence grow with realised variance.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
provenance.evidence: Explains why TQQQ exposure should be reduced when its own realised volatility is high: the drag term is proportional to Σr², which is exactly the state variable used in the throttle.

provenance.idea: TQQQ seeks 3× the daily index return, not 3× over longer periods; volatile markets can produce multi-day returns far from 3× and large drawdowns.
provenance.source: ProShares / TQQQ UltraPro QQQ Summary Prospectus
provenance.evidence: Primary-document confirmation of the daily-reset and holding-period risk that the vol throttle is designed to manage.

provenance.idea: A long moving-average trend filter (10-month/200-day style) keeps most of the equity return with much smaller drawdowns.
provenance.source: Faber (2007) / A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
provenance.evidence: The 165-day QQQ SMA regime is inherited from the round-1 winner, which follows this trend-filter literature; this strategy does not re-optimise the SMA.

provenance.idea: Leveraged equity can be held while the index is above its long average and moved to T-bills below it.
provenance.source: Gayed & Bilello (2016) / Leverage for the Long Run
provenance.evidence: Supports the regime-plus-leverage structure inherited from the winner; the round-2 contribution is only the sizing overlay.

provenance.idea: Volatility targeting reduces drawdowns; average exposure falls when volatility is high.
provenance.source: Man Group / The Impact of Volatility Targeting
provenance.evidence: Practitioner summary of the same mechanism; used as a cross-check, not as the primary evidence.

provenance.idea: The exact 30% core, 65% target, 20-day window and 2% band were chosen from the local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL parameter surface.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: The surface is monotone in the target (45/55/65/80% gives 10y CAGR 49.50/53.40/56.14/58.13% and DD 32.21/36.51/39.92/43.31%). The 30% core is the round middle of a flat 20–40% plateau (10y CAGR 56.71/57.05/57.31%, DD 40.77/41.32/41.82%); it was not fitted to a single cell.

provenance.idea: The 165-day QQQ SMA regime, the armed 4% minute stop and the benchmark metrics are inherited from the round-1 winner.
provenance.source: Round-1 winner report (internal)
provenance.evidence: Winner: 58.80% / 44.56% (10y) and 49.88% / 33.49% (5y) at 1 bp. This strategy is an overlay on that exact rule set; the stop and regime were not changed.

rejectedSources.source: Grossman & Zhou (1993) / Optimal Investment Strategies for Controlling Drawdowns
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The implied drawdown-from-high exposure rule was tested as a 60-day drawdown throttle (w = 1 − 0.5×|DD60|, floor 25%): 10y 57.40% / 43.56%, 5y 48.70% / 32.99%, Calmar 1.32 / 1.48 versus the primary's 1.38 / 1.66. It cuts after the loss has happened and misses the rebound, so it is not used.

rejectedSources.source: Quantmemo / Drawdown Control
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The practical 'exposure decreasing in drawdown' rule is the same mechanism as the Grossman–Zhou test above. Tested and rejected: no Calmar gain, and the 10y drawdown falls only from 44.56% to 43.56% while CAGR falls 1.4 pp.

rejectedSources.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) / Time Series Momentum
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Trend-strength scaling was tested as w = 0.5 + 0.5×trend/4% (floor 50%, where trend = QQQ/SMA165 − 1): 10y 53.35% / 42.39%, 5y 43.46% / 33.46%. It is procyclical — smallest exactly at recovery starts (2019, 2020, 2023) — and lost 2–12 pp of CAGR with little drawdown benefit.

rejectedSources.source: Thorp (2006) / Kelly criterion, direct daily implementation
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The literal fractional Kelly rule 0.5×μ60/σ²60, capped at 100%, was tested: 10y 25.35% / 45.38%, 5y 18.03% / 39.46%. Daily μ and σ² estimates are too noisy and imply only 20–30% exposure; full Kelly is worse. Kelly survives only as the conceptual basis for the shrunk 30/70 blend, not as a direct sizing formula.

rejectedSources.source: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2012) / Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Listed on the current web page but not a source for this strategy. It is a leverage-aversion/risk-parity paper, was not used to design the vol-target throttle, and was not tested here. Remove it from the paper list rather than presenting it as provenance.

corrections: The page omits the 165-day QQQ SMA regime. It must state: if QQQ's prior close is below its 165-day SMA, the next session is 100% BIL; the volatility sizing applies only on risk-on sessions. As written, 'residual BIL' implies an always-invested book, which is wrong.

The decision text 'Signals use only data through the current bar' is inaccurate. Daily signals use the prior session's close (regime and 20-day vol); only the stop uses the current 1-minute close; every target fills at the next bar's open (09:31 for the first bar). Truncation at 2022-01-03 leaves all prior weights bit-identical.

The rules omit the stop's arm condition and holding period: it is armed only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA × 1.01, and after a 4% stop the book stays in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night, re-entering next session if the regime is on.

The '70% sleeve at a 65% volatility target' phrasing should be written as w_TQQQ = 0.30 + 0.70 × min(1, 0.65/vol20) with BIL residual. The 70% is the weight on the vol-target signal, not a sleeve that is always 70% invested; when vol > 65% part of the sleeve is in BIL.

Paper list: remove Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2012) — it is not a source and was not tested. Replace the four generic 'doi.org' labels with their citations (Moreira–Muir DOI, Harvey JPM DOI, Cederburg DOI, Bongaerts DOI) and add Cheng & Madhavan (2009) for the 3× volatility-drag premise. Grossman–Zhou, Thorp and Moskowitz et al. belong in tested/rejected, not inspiration.

The verdict should include the thin 10y margin: 57.05% vs the 56.80% floor is a 0.25 pp cushion, and the 20% core neighbour is 56.71% and misses. Rolling return wins are 22/27 vs the winner's 23/27, so the consistency gain is drawdown, not return.

strategies.name: Risk-parity vol target
strategies.tagline: A 70% volatility cap on TQQQ, the rest in QQQ, and a 4% minute stop as the crash brake.
strategies.summary: Sizes the TQQQ sleeve at min(1, 0.70 / 20-day realised vol of TQQQ), puts the remainder of the risk-on sleeve in QQQ, and holds 100% BIL when QQQ is below its 165-day SMA. A 4% intraday stop, armed only when QQQ's first minute is below its 20-day SMA x 1.01, liquidates the TQQQ sleeve to BIL for the rest of the session and the following night. HRP and plain inverse-vol across QQQ/TQQQ/BIL were implemented and rejected: both collapse to roughly 99% BIL because BIL's variance is about four orders of magnitude smaller, and QQQ/TQQQ are 0.9999 correlated.
strategies.decision: At the close of session k-1, compute the 165-day SMA of QQQ closes and the 20-day realised vol of TQQQ from daily closes. For session k: risk-on if QQQ's prior close is above the SMA165, else 100% BIL. On risk-on sessions, TQQQ weight = min(1, 0.70 / sigma_TQQQ,20d) and the remainder of the sleeve is QQQ. At 09:30 the stop is armed if QQQ's first-minute price is below the 20-day SMA (through the prior close) times 1.01; if TQQQ then trades 4% below the session open, the TQQQ sleeve is sold at the next minute's open and the proceeds sit in BIL for the rest of the session and overnight. Every target is filled at the next bar's open with a 2% rebalance band and 1 bp slippage per side.
rules: Regime: for session k, risk-on if and only if QQQ's prior session close is above its 165-day SMA computed through the prior close; otherwise the portfolio is 100% BIL.
Risk-on sizing: TQQQ weight = min(1, 0.70 / sigma_TQQQ,20d), where sigma is annualised from the last 20 daily closes and lagged one session; the remainder of the sleeve is QQQ.
Stop arming: on a risk-on session, arm the stop only when QQQ's first-minute price is below its 20-day SMA (through the prior close) times 1.01.
Stop execution: if armed and TQQQ trades 4% below the session open, sell the TQQQ sleeve at the next minute's open and hold the proceeds in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.
Re-entry: the next session restarts from the daily target if the regime is still risk-on; weights are re-derived every session, not held until a discrete event.
Constraints: long-only, weights sum to <= 1, 2% trade band, fills at the next bar's open, 1 bp per side (5 bp and 10 bp were not measured).
strategies.verdict: Best 1 bp Calmar in the family (1.35 on 10y, 1.64 on 5y) and strict 5y dominance over the round-1 winner (+0.18 pp CAGR, -2.99 pp DD), but 5/10 bp were never measured and the fully cost-tested variant (RP-half) misses the 5y 2 pp band by 0.2 pp. Not promotable on current evidence.

provenance.idea: Scale exposure by trailing realised variance instead of holding a fixed leverage all the time: w = target / sigma.
provenance.source: Moreira & Muir (2017), Volatility-Managed Portfolios
provenance.evidence: The promoted rule min(1, 0.70 / sigma_TQQQ,20d) is a capped inverse-variance sizing rule in this spirit. We used daily-close 20-day realised vol, lagged one session, and applied the cap at 100% TQQQ. We did not re-test the paper's cross-sectional claim.

provenance.idea: Risk parity / equal risk contribution as the allocation principle across assets.
provenance.source: Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2012), Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity
provenance.evidence: Motivated the ERC/inverse-vol tests. On this asset set the literal rule gives 1.03% QQQ / 0.34% TQQQ / 98.63% BIL, so only the risk-budgeting idea survived into the vol target; the equal-risk portfolio itself was rejected.

provenance.idea: A 3x daily-reset ETF is the same factor at 3x leverage, so QQQ/TQQQ is a leverage choice, not a diversifier; multi-day returns are path-dependent.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009), The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
provenance.evidence: Explains why the QQQ/TQQQ covariance matrix is near-singular. Verified empirically on this data: 10-year daily correlation 0.99951, average 60-day correlation 0.99986, annualised vols 22.6% (QQQ) and 67.4% (TQQQ).

provenance.idea: A stop-loss rule adds value when returns exhibit momentum or regime shifts, and costs little when they do not.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014), When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses?
provenance.evidence: The 4% intraday stop and the MA20 arming gate are inherited unchanged from the round-1 winner; this paper is the theoretical license, not a result re-tested in this agent. The stop is a shared overlay, not the risk-parity contribution.

provenance.idea: 165-day SMA regime, 4% stop level, 70% vol target, 50/50 stop split.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: The 165-day window and 4% stop are round-1 parameters; the 70% target sits in the middle of the stable 0.70-0.85 region of the vol-target surface. No external source prescribes these values.

rejectedSources.source: Lopez de Prado (2016), Building Diversified Portfolios that Outperform Out-of-Sample (HRP)

It allocated 99.99% to BIL (QQQ 0.0089%, TQQQ 0.0010%), i.e. a T-bill portfolio, because BIL's variance is about four orders of magnitude smaller than TQQQ's. It did not change the rule, but it is the main reason the page should not upgrade the status beyond Alternative while 5/10 bp are unmeasured.

corrections: Rules are incomplete: the page says 'stop proceeds BIL' but never defines the stop. Add that on risk-on sessions the stop is armed when QQQ's first minute is below its 20-day SMA times 1.01, and that it sells the TQQQ sleeve at the next minute's open if TQQQ trades 4% below the session open, staying in BIL for the rest of the session and overnight. Without this the page describes a strategy that does not exist.

Fix the timing sentence. 'Signals use only data through the current bar' should read: the daily signals (SMA165 and 20-day vol) use closes through the prior session only and are lagged one session; the only current-session input is the 09:30 arming check. All targets fill at the next bar's open. As written the page implies a same-bar signal and fill, i.e. look-ahead, which the code does not do.

HRP is mis-attributed. Lopez de Prado (2016) is listed as a supporting paper, but HRP was implemented and rejected (99.99% BIL; QQQ/TQQQ average 60-day correlation 0.99986). It explains why the strategy is a vol target rather than a risk-parity portfolio, so it should be labelled 'tested and rejected', not cited as support.

The mechanism in the summary is slightly wrong: HRP collapses to BIL mainly because BIL's variance is about four orders of magnitude smaller than the equity sleeve's, not because QQQ/TQQQ are highly correlated. The 0.9999 correlation matters for the within-equity split (about 90/10 QQQ/TQQQ) and for why QQQ/TQQQ is not diversification.
State the risk-off leg explicitly: when QQQ is below its 165-day SMA the portfolio is 100% BIL. The current rules only say 'QQQ 165-day regime'.

strategies.name: ML crash overlay
strategies.tagline: A walk-forward 20-day crash classifier overlaid on the round-1 winner.
strategies.summary: The base is the round-1 winner: 100% TQQQ while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA, BIL otherwise, with an armed 4% minute stop. A 34-feature L2 logistic model, retrained annually on a 750-session rolling window with a 21-session purge, estimates the probability that TQQQ falls more than 15% over the next 20 sessions. If that probability ranks in the top decile of its trailing 252 sessions and the base would hold TQQQ at the next open, the session is moved to BIL. Headline metrics beat the winner at 1 bp and 5 bp, but the model's out-of-sample AUC is near 0.5 and the edge is concentrated in 2020 and 2026.
strategies.decision: At the close of session d, build 34 causal features from 1-minute bars through that close, impute and standardise them with training-window statistics only, and predict P(20-session TQQQ close-to-close return < -15%) with an L2 logistic model trained on the prior 750 sessions and retrained each calendar year (purge 21 sessions). Convert the probability to a trailing 252-session percentile rank. If rank >= 0.90 and the base regime would hold TQQQ at the next open, set the next session's target to 100% BIL; otherwise keep the base target. All targets fill at the next bar's open; the base's armed 4% minute stop continues to operate on non-overridden sessions.
rules: Base: QQQ prior close above its 165-day SMA -> 100% TQQQ, else 100% BIL. On risk-on sessions, arm a 4% stop from the session open only when QQQ's first-minute price is below its 20-day SMA times 1.01; if armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL through the night.

Features (34, all causal through the decision close): 1m realized vol and its 252-day percentile, 5/20/60-day vol ratios, 1m skew and 20-day mean skew, downside vol, VWAP distance, drawdown from the day high, first-30 and last-30 minute returns, close location in the range, overnight gap and 20-day mean gap, intraday return, up-day fraction, 20/252-day drawdown, distance from SMA20/SMA165, RSI(14), 5/20-day TQQQ leverage decay, BIL 5-day return, day-of-week, day range and 20-day mean range, volume ratio and z-score, and two interactions.

Model: L2 logistic regression (lambda 10), label = TQQQ 20-session close-to-close return below -15%; 750-session rolling training window, annual retrain, purge of horizon+1 = 21 sessions at the train/test boundary; median impute, standardise and winsorise at +/-6 sd using the training window only.

Overlay: if the predicted probability ranks in the top decile (>= 0.90) of its trailing 252 sessions and the base would hold TQQQ at the next open, the next session is 100% BIL. The overlay never adds TQQQ or QQQ exposure on base-BIL days; it is a one-session de-risking of an otherwise-long position.
Execution: long-only TQQQ/BIL, weights set at a bar and filled at the next bar's open, 2% no-trade band, 1 bp primary cost with 5 bp and 10 bp reported.
strategies.verdict: Headline 72.24%/41.50% (10y) and 53.10%/31.67% (5y) beats the winner at 1 bp and 5 bp, but the model's out-of-sample AUC is about 0.50 and the P&L is not clearly beyond a random-flag placebo (p95 65.7%, max 73.3%). The 10y edge is heavily 2020-dependent (ex-2020 50.0% vs the winner's 48.2%) and the 5y edge is entirely the 2026 selloff; fragile, do not treat as confirmed.

provenance.idea: Armed 4% intraday stop from the session open, only when QQQ is below its 20-day MA times 1.01.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014) / When do stop-loss rules stop losses?

strategies.name: Late-rally overlay
strategies.tagline: An additive last-hour overlay on the 165-day TQQQ winner, not a standalone trade.
strategies.summary: The base is the round-1 winner: hold 100% TQQQ while QQQ's prior close is above its 165-day SMA, otherwise BIL, with a 4% minute stop armed when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA x 1.01. On risk-off sessions only, if QQQ is up more than 1.5% from the prior close by 14:59, the strategy buys TQQQ at the 15:00 open and sells at the 15:59 open, then stays in BIL overnight. The overlay adds 96 one-hour trades over the 2017-2026 test window. The headline 67.92%/41.50% is the winner plus this overlay, not the overlay alone.
strategies.decision: Daily regime uses QQQ's prior close vs its 165-day SMA. On a risk-off session the 14:59 QQQ close (bar 329) is compared with the prior session's close; if the return is above +1.5%, the target is set at the 14:59 bar and filled at the 15:00 open. TQQQ is held through the 15:58 bar; at the 15:58 close the target is set back to BIL and filled at the 15:59 open, so the 15:59-16:00 final minute and the overnight are not held. On risk-on sessions the winner's rules run unchanged, including the armed 4% stop, which fills at the next minute's open.
rules: Base regime: hold 100% TQQQ while QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA; otherwise hold 100% BIL.

Base stop: on risk-on days, arm a 4% stop from the session open only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA x 1.01; if armed and TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the night.
Overlay signal: on a risk-off session, compute run60 = QQQ 14:59 close / QQQ prior close - 1; if run60 > +1.5%, buy TQQQ at the 15:00 open.
Overlay exit: sell at the 15:59 open (target set at the 15:58 close) and stay in BIL overnight; the 15:59-16:00 final minute is not held.
Long-only, weights sum to <= 1, next-bar-open fills; no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ.
strategies.verdict: Beats the round-1 winner on CAGR in both windows at 1/5/10 bp, cuts 10y max DD by about 3 pp and ties the 5y DD; at 10 bp it is 52.61%/46.59% (10y) and 42.46%/34.93% (5y). But the edge is fragile: 96 events, 52 of them in 2022, none in 2017 or 2021, and the overlay is slightly behind the winner in 2023-26 (66.79% vs 67.76%). Treat it as a small, uncorrelated add-on, not a new standalone engine.

provenance.idea: Leveraged ETF daily rebalancing creates predictable end-of-day demand in the underlying, proportional to L(L-1) times the day's return, which can amplify late-day moves.
provenance.source: Barbon et al. (2022) / Liquidity Provision to Leveraged ETFs and Equity Options Rebalancing Flows: Evidence from End-of-Day Stock Prices
provenance.evidence: The paper shows LETF rebalancing and option delta-hedging exert economically large price pressure on end-of-day returns and links LETF flows to last-half-hour stock returns. This motivated testing the 15:00-16:00 window, not the exact 1.5% threshold.

provenance.idea: LETF rebalancing concentrates near the close and is associated with higher end-of-day volatility, so the last 30-60 minutes are the right place to look for a flow effect.
provenance.source: Shum, Hejazi, Haryanto & Rodier (2016) / Intraday Share Price Volatility and Leveraged ETF Rebalancing
provenance.evidence: Review of Finance 20(6):2379-2409. Documents end-of-day rebalancing activity and end-of-day volatility. It supports the timing of the test but is about volatility, not directional continuation.

provenance.idea: Intraday momentum: the day's move can predict the last part of the session, so a late-day continuation rule is plausible.
provenance.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) / Market intraday momentum
provenance.evidence: Journal of Financial Economics 129(2):394-414. Shows the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return. Our rule is a regime-gated variant conditioned on the move from the prior close at 14:59.

provenance.idea: The opposite hypothesis: intraday losers outperform into the close (end-of-day reversal), which would argue against buying late-day rallies.
provenance.source: Vidovich & Zerjal (2026) / The End-of-Day Reversal After 2019: A Pre-Registered Test on S&P 500 Stocks Excluding Heavily Traded Names (related to Baltussen, Da & Soebhag, 2025)
provenance.evidence: Documents an end-of-day reversal through 2019, weaker after 2019. We tested it on QQQ risk-off days: on strong rally days the last hour continued up (mean +64 bp TQQQ), not reversed. The overnight after those rallies did reverse (mean -90 bp), which is consistent with temporary end-of-day pressure.

provenance.idea: Caution: the LETF late-day effect may be statistically detectable but economically small, so it should not be treated as a proven source of alpha.
provenance.source: Lenkey (2024) / The market impact of leveraged ETFs: A survey of the literature
provenance.evidence: Quantitative Finance and Economics 8(4):815-840. The survey concludes that reported associations are statistically significant but the economic associations appear insignificant and many papers have methodological issues. It is a caution, not support for a tradeable late-day flow.

provenance.idea: Caution: LETF rebalancing may not actually amplify late-day returns or volatility.
provenance.source: Ivanov & Lenkey (2018) / Do leveraged ETFs really amplify late-day returns and volatility?
provenance.evidence: Journal of Financial Markets 41:36-56, cited in the Lenkey survey. Finds little evidence of amplification, which is why the local event study is the primary evidence and the flow mechanism is only an interpretation.

provenance.idea: Background mechanics: constant-leverage ETFs must rebalance daily, which is the accounting basis for the flow story.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) / The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
provenance.evidence: Explains daily constant-leverage rebalancing mechanics. It does not establish a directional last-hour continuation and was not used to calibrate the rule. The web page's SSRN 1393995 link was not verified.

provenance.idea: Base rules: 165-day QQQ SMA regime plus the armed 4% minute stop.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Inherited from the round-1 winner and replicated exactly on the local adjusted 1m QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel: 58.80%/44.56% (10y) and 49.88%/33.49% (5y) at 1 bp.

provenance.idea: Overlay rules: 1.5% run-up threshold, 15:00-15:59 execution, BIL overnight.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Measured on the local 1m panel. The threshold was chosen from a sweep on the same sample; thresholds from 0.5% to 3.0% all improved the winner, and the 2017-2026 test window contains 96 events (52 of them in 2022).

strategies.name: Volume-armed TQQQ crash stop
strategies.tagline: The round-1 165-day QQQ regime and 4% minute stop, with the stop honoured only when the session's relative volume is at least normal and always armed on high-volume days.
strategies.summary: A 165-day QQQ SMA regime holds 100% TQQQ (else 100% BIL). On risk-on sessions a 4% stop from the session open liquidates to BIL at the next minute's open and stays out for the rest of the day and the night. The only new element is how the stop is armed: it is honoured at minute i only when cumulative QQQ volume divided by its prior-20-day same-time-of-day mean (rvol) is above 1.0, and it is additionally armed when rvol exceeds 1.5 even if QQQ is above its 20-day MA. Quiet-day breaks are treated as liquidity air pockets; high-volume breaks are treated as information. Long-only, one asset at a time, 100% TQQQ or 100% BIL; 195 stop events over ten years, about 82 fills a year.
strategies.decision: The regime uses QQQ's close on day d-1 versus its 165-day SMA, so the state for day d is fixed before the open. On a risk-on day the stop compares the current one-minute TQQQ close with the TQQQ 09:30 open and subtracts 4%; the arming condition compares the QQQ 09:30 price with MA20 of prior closes times 1.01 and reads rvol at the same bar i (cumulative volume 09:30..i over the prior-20-day mean of the same cumulative quantity at the same minute). If the stop fires at bar i, weight goes to 0 and fills at the open of bar i+1; the position then stays in BIL through the close and the overnight and is re-established at the next session's open if the regime is still on. Every weight is set at bar i from data through bar i and executed at bar i+1's open; the regime, MA20 and the 20-day volume baseline all use prior sessions only.
rules: Regime (daily): QQQ prior close above its 165-day SMA -> hold 100% TQQQ for the next session, including overnight; otherwise hold 100% BIL.

Stop: while risk-on and long TQQQ, if the TQQQ 1-minute close falls 4% below the session's 09:30 open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.

Relative volume: rvol(i) = cumulative QQQ volume from 09:30 through bar i, divided by the mean of the same cumulative quantity over the prior 20 sessions at the same minute of day (rolling 20-day mean shifted one day, so today is excluded).

Arming: the stop is honoured at bar i only if rvol(i) > 1.0, and it is additionally armed when rvol(i) > 1.5 even if QQQ is above its 20-day MA. Formally: armed = (QQQ@09:30 < MA20(prev) x 1.01 OR rvol > 1.5) AND rvol > 1.0.
Re-entry: after a stop the position is re-established at the next session's open if the regime is still risk-on; no intraday re-entry, no shorting, no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ.
Execution and costs: next-bar-open fills, long-only, weights sum to at most 1; 1 bp primary, 5 bp and 10 bp reported. 801 fills over 10 years (about 82 per year) versus 657 for the round-1 winner.
strategies.verdict: Strictly dominates the round-1 winner on headline metrics at 1, 5 and 10 bp in both windows (65.90/42.49 and 53.17/28.64 at 1 bp; 60.56/45.45 and 48.80/29.35 at 5 bp; 54.14/48.93 and 43.52/30.26 at 10 bp, versus 58.80/44.56 and 49.88/33.49 at 1 bp), and 21 of 28 rolling 3-year windows beat the winner's CAGR. But the label is Fragile, not Leader: the 5-year drawdown gain is a single event. Restoring the one 2026-06-24 stop that the volume floor suppressed (a -4% break on 0.87x normal volume) moves the 5-year result to 50.72/34.16 - a drawdown 0.67 pp worse than the winner. The 10-year leg is genuinely robust: it survives every value of both new volume parameters (floor 0.90-1.10, re-arm 1.2-2.0) and of the arming MA (10-50), and the gain is the intended one (the re-arm fires on 2020-02-20 and 2020-02-21, the day after QQQ's February 2020 high, before the slow regime flips; 2020 is +267.9% versus the winner's +183.9%). It is also dominated by the round-2 ratio-froth leader on both windows, so it is an alternative sleeve rather than the leader.

provenance.idea: A stop-loss rule adds value when returns have momentum and costs little when they do not - the licence for carrying an intraday stop at all.
provenance.source: Kaminski, K. M., & Lo, A. W. (2014) / When do stop-loss rules stop losses? (Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254)
provenance.evidence: Shows analytically and empirically that stop-loss policies improve expected returns under momentum/regime-switching return processes and are roughly neutral otherwise. Used to justify keeping the round-1 stop and treating its whipsaw cost as the price of a tail hedge, not as evidence the stop is broken. No parameter taken from the paper.

provenance.idea: Intraday momentum is stronger on high-volume days - i.e. volume conditions whether a price move is informative, which is the direct basis for arming the stop on rvol > 1.5.
provenance.source: Gao, L., Han, Y., Li, S. Z., & Zhou, G. (2018) / Market intraday momentum (Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 394-414)
provenance.evidence: Reports that the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return and that the predictability is stronger on more volatile and higher-volume days. The conditional claim (volume strengthens the signal) inspired the rvol > 1.5 re-arming clause. Their direct rule was tested separately and did NOT reproduce on QQQ 2017-2026 (corr +0.022, top-minus-bottom quintile +4 bp, and the volume-confirmed 5m version earns -1.06 bp per trade before cost) - see rejected_sources.

provenance.idea: Low-volume price moves are the persistent ones and high-volume moves are late-stage and reverse faster - the basis for refusing to honour a stop on a below-normal-volume break.
provenance.source: Lee, C. M. C., & Swaminathan, B. (2000) / Price momentum and trading volume (Journal of Finance 55(5), 2017-2069)
provenance.evidence: Documents that high-volume winners reverse faster while low-volume winners show greater persistence (the momentum life cycle). Used qualitatively, as the reason a quiet -4% dip should be treated as noise and a heavy-volume -4% dip as a breakdown. This is cross-sectional monthly stock evidence, not index intraday evidence, and I did not attempt to replicate their portfolio sort; the mapping to a 1-minute stop is an analogy, which is why confidence is medium.

provenance.idea: Order-flow imbalance explains short-horizon price changes (average event-level R^2 of 65%), so an intraday flow proxy should be able to time turns.
provenance.source: Cont, R., Kukanov, A., & Stoikov, S. (2014) / The price impact of order book events (Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 47-88)
provenance.evidence: Used to justify testing flow-based intraday signals. Implemented as close-location-value signed volume (a 1-minute proxy for signed flow, since the data has no bid/ask) and as a 5-minute variant. Result: no forward predictive power at this resolution (corr -0.010 at 1m, +0.001 at 5m against the next 30-minute TQQQ return). Their R^2 is contemporaneous, not predictive, which is the likely reason the proxy failed.

provenance.idea: Order imbalance predicts individual stock returns and persists at short lags.
provenance.source: Chordia, T., & Subrahmanyam, A. (2004) / Order imbalance and individual stock returns (Journal of Financial Economics 72(3), 485-518)
provenance.evidence: Provided the prior that lagged imbalance carries information. My proxy (CLV-weighted volume, and a tick-rule signed-volume variant) showed no usable forward power on QQQ/TQQQ at 1 or 5 minutes; the effect in the paper is daily and cross-sectional, which does not transfer to a single index ETF intraday.

provenance.idea: Abnormally high trading volume predicts a short-horizon return premium (high-volume return premium).
provenance.source: Gervais, S., Kaniel, R., & Mingelgrin, D. H. (2001) / The high-volume return premium (Journal of Finance 56(3), 877-919)
provenance.evidence: Motivated a check of whether high-rvol days predict higher forward returns. On QQQ the effect is absent at the relevant horizons and reverses intraday: high-rvol days are followed by worse overnights in the pooled sample (rvol>1.5 and down: -74.9 bp), but that is a 2020 artifact and the sign flips by era. The cross-country replication is cited only as the modern confirmation of the premium I could not find here.

provenance.idea: VWAP is an execution benchmark, not a forecast - it is the price an average participant achieved, which is why deviation from it need not predict returns.
provenance.source: Konishi, H. (2002) / Optimal slice of a VWAP trade (Journal of Financial Markets 5(2), 197-221)
provenance.evidence: Used to frame the VWAP-deviation test. VWAP is defined and studied as a liquidation benchmark to be tracked; nothing in the literature treats deviation from it as a return signal. Consistent with my finding that close/VWAP-1 has essentially zero forward correlation (-0.009 at 1m, +0.007 at 5m).

provenance.idea: VWAP tracking is an execution problem with closed-form optimal schedules; no return predictability is claimed.
provenance.source: Frei, C., & Westray, N. (2015) / Optimal execution of a VWAP order: a stochastic control approach (Mathematical Finance 25(3), 612-639)
provenance.evidence: Second confirmation that the VWAP literature is about minimising slippage to a benchmark, not about forecasting. Cited in the report to explain why the VWAP-deviation signal should not be expected to work, and it did not.

provenance.idea: A VWAP-deviation mean-reversion strategy has been proposed but not backtested.
provenance.source: Bhatti, A. (2026) / Momentum exhaustion and fair value reversion: an ADX-conditioned VWAP strategy (SSRN 6454659)
provenance.evidence: The abstract proposes trading reversion toward VWAP after momentum exhaustion and states that formal backtesting and performance attribution are left to future work. I ran the testable core (VWAP deviation, with and without a trend filter): no edge. Cited as the clearest statement that the practitioner idea is untested rather than contradicted.

provenance.idea: Essentially all of TQQQ's drift is earned overnight, so any minute-level rule can only be a small overlay on an overnight position.
provenance.source: Lou, D., Polk, C., & Skouras, S. (2019) / A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns (Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213)
provenance.evidence: Inherited from the round-1 winner, not re-derived here, but it is the reason the new rule conditions an existing stop instead of adding intraday trading. My own decomposition on this data matches it: TQQQ overnight +1,354.8% versus intraday +81.2% over 2017-2026.

provenance.idea: The exact thresholds rvol > 1.0 (floor) and rvol > 1.5 (re-arm), and the decision to gate the stop rather than trade on volume.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Chosen from a two-dimensional surface on the local 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL data, not from a paper. The floor is interpretable as 'participation at least normal' and the surface is flat from 0.90 to 1.10 (10y CAGR 65.0-69.0%, 5y DD 27.8-30.4%), so the exact 1.0 is not a tuned optimum. The re-arm level is flat from 1.2 to 2.0. Both are disclosed as data-chosen in the report.

rejectedSources.source: Own test (mandate family): overnight exit after a high-relative-volume session (the most promising volume idea found)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Pooled, it looks strong: rvol>1.5 days are followed by -74.9 bp (down days) and -124.4 bp (up days) of overnight TQQQ return versus +25 to +35 bp otherwise, corr -0.19, and it is not explained by 20-day volatility (corr -0.001). It is not robust. Era spreads: 2017-2019 -0.05%, 2020-2021 -0.23%, 2022-2026 +0.06%; in the 5y window high-volume nights were better (+0.236% vs +0.155%). Applied to the winner the gate gives 57.35/44.52 (10y) but 41.08/36.14 (5y) at rvol>1.5, i.e. it destroys 8.8 pp of 5y CAGR. The pooled average is a 2020 artifact.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: 1-minute and 5-minute order-flow proxies (CLV-signed volume, tick-rule signed volume, up/down-volume pressure, VWAP deviation, cumulative RVOL)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: No forward power after costs. Correlations with the next 30-minute TQQQ return: CLV flow -0.010, VWAP deviation -0.009, cumulative RVOL -0.047, 1-bar RVOL +0.007, 5m flow +0.001, 5m VWAP dev +0.007, 5m cumulative RVOL +0.006 (n = 129k-155k each). The -0.047 is non-monotone and contrarian (bottom quintile +35 bp, top quintile -52 bp), does not reproduce by era (2017-19 ~0.00, 2020-21 +0.03, 2022-26 +0.04), and 30 bp of spread does not survive ~2 bp of round-trip cost.

rejectedSources.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) applied directly: volume-confirmed intraday momentum (first half-hour predicts last half-hour, stronger on high volume)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Tested on QQQ 2017-2026 and absent at this resolution: corr(first-30m, last-30m TQQQ) = +0.022, top-minus-bottom quintile +4 bp; the high-RVOL split does have the right sign (corr +0.043, +23 bp top-minus-bottom) but it is a noisy top-quintile sort and vanishes when conditioned on the sign of the first half hour. A direct volume-confirmed 5m momentum trade (long TQQQ 30 minutes when the last 5m return is positive and 5m RVOL > 1.2) earns -1.06 bp per trade before cost and -3.06 bp after. I kept only the qualitative insight (volume conditions informativeness), not the trading rule.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: distribution-day counting (IBD-style) - count days down >0.2% on rising volume over 20-30 sessions, de-risk at 4-6 days
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Destroys the return. The count keeps the book out of TQQQ 43-95% of the time: dd20<4 gives 16.83/34.03, dd25<5 gives 9.14/38.23, dd30<4 gives 3.87/16.99 (10y). Even with the winner's stop layered on top, dd25<5 returns 10.21/35.41. The rule is a growth-stock market-top heuristic and does not survive a long-only leveraged-ETF application.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: volume-based regime (165-day VWAP instead of SMA, plus OBV>MA and A-D>MA confirmation filters)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: No improvement. 165-day volume-weighted price regime: 47.08/58.03 (10y) and 30.49/44.94 (5y) versus SMA 46.63/58.76 and 36.14/42.17. Adding OBV>MA165: 28.24/61.09. Adding A-D>MA20: 26.46/43.07. The price SMA dominates the volume-weighted variants, so volume was not used at the daily gate.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: continuous volume-scaled stop, stop_i = 4% x (1 + c x (1 - rvol_i))
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Smooth but worse than the discrete rule. Best point (S=3.5%, c=0.3) gives 61.77/47.68 (10y) and 53.54/32.84 (5y): better 5y, worse 10y than the winner. At S=4% the whole c grid is worse than the winner on at least one metric. Rejected in favour of the binary arming rule, which has a cleaner interpretation.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: volume at the stop bar as a crash-versus-wick classifier (decide whether a stop was 'right' using rvol at the trigger)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Post-stop drift is not monotone in rvol. Quartile means of stop-to-next-open return: -1.61%, -0.76%, +0.49%, -0.08% (n = 29 per bucket, 4% ungated stop). The lowest-volume stops were the worst ones, which is the opposite of the 'quiet dips are noise' story at the event level. Only the day-level floor rule survived; a per-event classifier did not.

rejectedSources.source: Own test: volume-spike reversal - buy after a 1-minute QQQ drop >0.5% on 1-minute RVOL > 10
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Only 6 events in 10 years, +228 bp over the next 30 minutes. Too rare to build on, the threshold was chosen after seeing the data, and the strategy is long-only and already fully invested so there is nothing to buy.

rejectedSources.source: Trading Studio (2026) / Volume-confirmed momentum on US stocks, 2001-2025: 7.92% CAGR vs 8.59% for SPY
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Not rejected as a source - used as external counter-evidence for the negative result. The practitioner version of volume-confirmed momentum (top-30 12-month momentum filtered on rising 3-month volume) underperforms SPY over 24.5 years with a -61% max drawdown, which is the same sign as my own intraday test. Cited in the report as a sanity check that the volume-confirmation idea is weaker in practice than in the papers.

corrections: Status must not be 'Leader'. The round-2 ratio-froth leader (69.50/39.11 on 10y, 63.74/26.85 on 5y at 1 bp) dominates this strategy on both windows. This is an alternative sleeve: Fragile, not Leader.

Do not describe this as a VWAP or order-flow strategy. The report's actual finding is that every directional VWAP/order-flow signal was rejected (corr -0.010 for CLV flow, -0.009 for VWAP deviation, 0.001-0.007 at 5 minutes). The surviving rule only uses volume to decide whether to honour an existing stop. If any copy says 'trades VWAP deviation' or 'uses order-flow imbalance', it is wrong.

Do not present the 5-year drawdown improvement as robust. It is one event: the volume floor suppressed the 2026-06-24 stop (a -4% break on 0.87x normal volume), and restoring that single stop moves the 5-year result from 53.17/28.64 to 50.72/34.16 - a drawdown 0.67 pp worse than the round-1 winner. Quote 28.64% only with that caveat attached.

The 10-year improvement IS robust and can be presented plainly: it survives every value of the floor (0.90-1.10), the re-arm threshold (1.2-2.0) and the arming MA (10-50). The one sensitivity is the inherited stop distance: shortening to 3.0-3.5% raises 10y drawdown to 48.4%/45.4%.

LEADER.md lines 76 and 78 list 'Ratio + volume 50/50' (68.14/40.80 and 58.69/27.74) and 'First-hour + volume 50/50' (67.83/35.63 and 53.10/32.02). Those are 50/50 blends of two sleeves, not this standalone strategy. Do not copy 58.69/27.74 or 53.10/32.02 onto this page; the standalone numbers are 65.90/42.49 and 53.17/28.64 at 1 bp.
LEADER.md line 95 describes this folder as the 'volume-armed stop sleeve' - that description is accurate and needs no correction.

Include the 10 bp row (54.14/48.93 on 10y, 43.52/30.26 on 5y). This strategy survives 10 bp in both windows, which is unusual for a stop overlay and is a genuine strength; omitting it undersells the result.

State the drawdown convention. Headline drawdowns are 1-minute equity marks; on daily closes they are 39.43% (10y) and 28.20% (5y). The round-1 winner is 44.56% minute / 41.62% daily. Do not mix the two conventions inside one comparison.
Quote fills as 801 over 10 years (361 over 5 years, about 82 per year), not 657 - 657 is the round-1 winner's count. The extra fills are the 46 stops that volume alone armed.

Rolling-window counts differ by agent because of the window grid. My grid is 28 quarterly-start 3-year windows from 2017-01: 26/28 beat TQQQ CAGR, 28/28 have lower drawdown than TQQQ, 21/28 beat the round-1 winner's CAGR, 14/28 have a lower drawdown than the winner. Do not quote LEADER.md's 27/27 or agent 21's 26/28 for this strategy.

Half-day sessions are handled by the last valid bar, so a 13:00 close works unchanged, but the 20-day same-time-of-day volume baseline treats a prior half-day's truncated cumulative volume as its late-minute value, biasing rvol up by roughly 5% on the session after a half-day. Immaterial for a 1.0/1.5 threshold; disclosed rather than corrected.

strategies.name: Gap-up fade overlay
strategies.tagline: Overlay on the winner: fade small gap-ups in a weak tape, then re-enter before the close.
strategies.summary: Standalone gap strategies fail because TQQQ's drift is overnight and intraday-only gap trades make only 2-9% CAGR. On top of the 165-day QQQ regime and the armed 4% minute stop, selling TQQQ at 09:31 on armed +0.15% to +0.50% gap-ups and buying back at 15:59 lifts 10-year CAGR from 58.80% to 65.17% and cuts max drawdown from 44.56% to 39.02%. The 5-year result is 54.92%/30.99%, but it is fragile to the arm-gate buffer and the per-event edge is not statistically significant.
strategies.decision: At 09:30 ET the strategy reads QQQ's opening gap (open vs prior close) and the first-minute close. If QQQ's prior close is above its 165-day SMA (risk-on), the 4% stop is armed when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01, and the gap is between +0.15% and +0.50%, it targets 100% BIL for the 09:30 bar; the harness fills at the 09:31 open. At 15:58 it targets 100% TQQQ for the 15:59 open unless TQQQ closed 4% below the session open at any bar through 15:58, in which case it stays in BIL overnight. Otherwise the base winner holds TQQQ overnight and uses the 4% armed stop.
rules: Regime: QQQ's prior daily close above its 165-day SMA means risk-on; otherwise hold 100% BIL.
On risk-on days, hold 100% TQQQ including overnight.

Arm the 4% stop only when QQQ's first-minute close is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01. While armed, if TQQQ closes 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.
Gap-up fade: on a risk-on, armed day with a QQQ opening gap between +0.15% and +0.50% versus the prior close, sell TQQQ at the 09:31 open and hold 100% BIL through 15:58.
Re-enter at the 15:59 open unless TQQQ closed 4% below the session open at any bar through 15:58; if it did, stay in BIL overnight.
Next session: re-enter at the open if the regime is still on. Long-only, no leverage beyond 1x TQQQ, no shorting.
strategies.verdict: Strictly dominates the winner at 1 bp and 5 bp on both windows (65.17/39.02 and 54.92/30.99 at 1 bp; 58.02/40.93 and 48.78/31.65 at 5 bp), but the 5-year pass depends on the winner's exact 1% arm gate and collapses at 0.5%/1.5%, and the per-event edge is not significant (t=1.60 over 10y, 0.92 over 5y). Treat the 10-year result as a robust crash-hedge overlay and the 5-year result as sample-specific.

provenance.idea: Small opening gaps fill; large gaps persist and continue. This size split is the reason to fade only the small-gap band and exclude large gap-ups.

strategies.name: Drawdown regime
strategies.tagline: De-risking on QQQ's drawdown fails; the one survivor halves the minute stop once QQQ is 8% below its 52-week high.
strategies.summary: The mandated overlay - exit to BIL when QQQ is 5/10/15% below its 52-week high - fails on every setting. The 165-day SMA already holds BIL for 80-84% of deep-drawdown sessions, and where the rule does bind, forward TQQQ returns are above average (+11.5% over 20 days in the -8..-12% bucket). The one rule that clears the round-2 bar keeps TQQQ but cuts the intraday stop from 4% to 2% while QQQ is at least 8% below its high: 61.57%/40.34% (10y) and 51.75%/31.63% (5y) at 1 bp, dominating the round-1 winner at 1/5/10 bp.
strategies.decision: Before each session, QQQ's drawdown from its trailing 252-session high is computed from closes through the prior session, so it is known before the open: dd = QQQ_close(t-1) / max(QQQ_close, t-252..t-1) - 1. The 165-day SMA regime (prior close vs prior SMA) selects TQQQ or BIL. If risk-on and dd <= -8%, the intraday stop is 2% instead of 4%. During the session an armed stop (QQQ first-minute price < prior 20-day SMA x 1.01) exits TQQQ at the next minute's open when the TQQQ close is below session open x (1 - stop); the book stays in BIL for the rest of the session and the night, and re-enters at the next session's open if the regime is still risk-on. Every target set at bar i is filled at bar i+1's open.
rules: Regime: if QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA, hold 100% TQQQ including overnight; otherwise hold 100% BIL.
Stop arming: on risk-on sessions only, arm the stop when QQQ's first-minute price is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01.

Stop: while armed, if TQQQ's minute close falls more than 4% below the session open (2% when QQQ is at least 8% below its 52-week high), sell at the next minute's open and hold BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.
Re-entry: at the next session's open if the 165-day regime is still risk-on; after a stop the position does not re-enter intraday.
Drawdown definition: QQQ close(t-1) / max(QQQ close, t-252..t-1) - 1, using only completed sessions through t-1.
Long-only, one position at a time, no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ; weights sum to <= 1.
strategies.verdict: Strictly dominates the round-1 winner at 1/5/10 bp and has lower drawdown in 82/82 rolling 3-year windows, but the return edge is not statistically significant (20-day block bootstrap p = 0.26), a 2% stop near the high also helps (placebo), and walk-forward parameter selection is neutral-to-worse. The mandated 5/10/15% de-risking gates are a clean negative; two of them even lose to TQQQ buy-and-hold on 10y CAGR.

strategies.name: Late-day de-risk
strategies.tagline: Sell TQQQ for the last 30 minutes when a risk-on day is more than 1% below its 09:30 open at 15:00.
strategies.summary: Runs the round-1 winner (QQQ 165-day SMA regime, 100% TQQQ risk-on / 100% BIL risk-off, plus the 4% intraday stop) and adds one conditional 30-minute de-risk: on a risk-on session where QQQ is more than 1% below its session open at 15:00, the TQQQ position is moved to BIL from the 15:01 open to the 15:30 open, then the overnight hold resumes. The premise is the daily-reset 3x fund's forced closing rebalance, which sells into a down close. It is a return overlay, not a drawdown fix: +2.55 pp of 10y CAGR and +3.58 pp of 5y CAGR at 1 bp, with 10y DD 44.18% vs 44.56% and 5y DD 33.50% vs 33.49%.
strategies.decision: Once per session, on the 15:00 bar close (15:00:59 ET), read q_day = QQQ(15:00) / QQQ(09:30 open) - 1. If the regime is risk-on (QQQ prior close > 165-day SMA) and the winner's 4% stop has not already fired and q_day < -1.0%, set the 15:00 bar's target to 100% BIL; that order fills at the 15:01 open. Restore the 100% TQQQ target on the 15:29 bar so the buy fills at the 15:30 open and the position is long into the close and overnight. If the stop already fired or the regime is off, the book is already in BIL and the overlay does nothing. All signals use bars through the 15:00 close; every fill is at the next bar's open.
rules: Regime gate: hold 100% TQQQ only while QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA; otherwise hold 100% BIL for the whole session.

Winner's stop: on a risk-on day armed when QQQ's first-minute price is below its 20-day SMA x 1.01, if TQQQ trades 4% below the session open, sell at the next minute's open and stay in BIL for the rest of the day and the night.
Late-day carve: at 15:00, if still long TQQQ and QQQ is more than 1% below the 09:30 open, sell TQQQ at the 15:01 open and hold BIL.
Buy TQQQ back at the 15:30 open and hold it overnight; risk-on days that do not trigger the carve are unchanged.
strategies.verdict: At 1 bp it beats the winner on both windows' return (+2.55 pp 10y, +3.58 pp 5y) with 10y DD 0.38 pp lower and 5y DD flat, and 26/27 rolling 3-year windows beat the winner. But 218 of 317 signal days are pre-empted by the winner's stop or the risk-off regime, leaving only ~10 executed trades a year (t = 1.97); 2026 was negative; at 5 bp the return gain is +0.20/+1.50 pp with worse DD; at 10 bp it loses. Treat it as a sub-2 bp execution tweak, not a robust alpha or a drawdown fix.

provenance.idea: Sell TQQQ for the 15:01-15:30 window on risk-on days when QQQ is more than 1% below its session open at 15:00, then buy back for the overnight hold.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Own 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ panel, 2017-2026. Gain per event = -(TQQQ 15:01 open to 15:30 open): 195 risk-on signal days, mean +19.99 bp, t = 3.02, win 57.6%; IS 2017-2021 +16.20 bp (t = 1.63, n = 106), OOS 2022-2026 +24.49 bp (t = 2.93, n = 89). Every threshold from 0% to -2% improves 10y CAGR at 1 bp. The rule is an empirical discovery from this data, not a published rule.

provenance.idea: A daily-reset leveraged ETF's closing rebalance is price-insensitive, executed at the close, and pushes the close in the direction of the day's move, creating end-of-day momentum.
provenance.source: Mathis & Moerke (2022) - Liquidity Provision to Leveraged ETFs and Equity Options Rebalancing Flows
provenance.evidence: The working paper documents 'large price pressure on end-of-day returns' when leveraged-ETF swap counterparties rebalance, states that 'leveraged ETFs contribute to a basket-wide momentum effect', that swap counterparties 'are required to establish the target exposure of the fund at the close', and that the leveraged-ETF effect is 'significantly decreasing' over time. The last point matches the 2024-2026 attenuation observed here.

provenance.idea: Late-day leveraged-ETF rebalancing price pressure exists in the academic literature, but its economic magnitude is disputed.
provenance.source: Lenkey (2024) - The market impact of leveraged ETFs: A survey of the literature, Quantitative Finance and Economics 8(4), 815-840
provenance.evidence: Survey of the late-day LETF literature. It reports statistically significant associations between rebalancing demand and late-day returns/volatility, but concludes that 'the economic associations appear to be insignificant' and that liquidity is generally sufficient. Used as a caution, not as support: it is a reason to keep the position small and the cost assumption conservative.

provenance.idea: The size of the forced rebalance is dE = L(L-1) * r * NAV, i.e. 6% of NAV per 1% of index return for a 3x fund.
provenance.source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009) - The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds
provenance.evidence: Standard derivation of the daily-reset trade used for the arithmetic in the report ('6% of NAV per 1% index move'). Referenced from the report text; the URL is left null because it was not fetched during this work.

provenance.idea: In a real selloff the leveraged QQQ complex has to sell billions into the close, and that flow lands in the closing auction.
provenance.source: ETF.com - One Bad Day: A levered-QQQ ETF Case Study
provenance.evidence: Walks through a specific down day for TQQQ/SQQQ and estimates roughly $12.8bn of TQQQ selling needed 'sometime between roughly 3:30 and the close'. Anecdotal but a concrete illustration of the mechanism.

provenance.idea: The reset flow is executed in or around the closing auction, so the pressure is concentrated in the last part of the session.
provenance.source: Strasmore - Leveraged ETF Rebalancing Into the Close
provenance.evidence: Gives the reset arithmetic (a 3x fund trades roughly six times the day's index move against NAV) and shows TQQQ printing about 0.36% of session volume in the closing cross and about 9.5% in the closing stretch. Consistent with a late-day, not all-day, effect.

provenance.idea: Market intraday momentum: the first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return, stronger on volatile days.
provenance.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) - Market Intraday Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 394-414
provenance.evidence: Tested the literal first-30-minutes predictor on this data: regressing the last-hour TQQQ return on the first-30-minute QQQ return gives beta +0.14 (t = 2.16) in 2017-2021 and -0.10 (t = -1.63) in 2022-2026, i.e. no stable rule. The day-so-far signal used here is a different, much stronger construction. The paper is related literature and the origin of the family, not the source of this rule.

rejectedSources.source: Vojtko & Dujava (2024) - Lunch Effect in the U.S. Stock Market Indices
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The 12:00-14:00 TQQQ mean is -2.92 bp in 2017-2021 and +3.78 bp in 2022-2026 (sign flip). The only stable lunch pattern is continuation after a >3% morning (+24 bp in both halves), which the winner already captures by staying long.

strategies.name: Overnight + first 30m
strategies.tagline: Hold TQQQ only from 15:59 to 10:01 the next morning, and only while QQQ is above its 165-day SMA with a 2% hysteresis band.
strategies.summary: Almost all of TQQQ's return accrues outside the cash session, and the last 30 minutes of the session are the worst block of the day. The strategy therefore owns TQQQ from the 15:59 open until the 10:01 open the next morning (overnight gap plus the first half hour), and holds cash the rest of the day. A daily QQQ 165-day SMA with a 2% hysteresis band switches the whole block off in downtrends, which is what produces the drawdown protection.
strategies.decision: Once per day, using only the previous day's QQQ close: regime ON if close > SMA165 * 1.02, OFF if close < SMA165 * 0.98, otherwise unchanged (hysteresis). If ON, a target of 100% TQQQ is written on the 15:58:00 bar and filled at the 15:59:00 open of the last bar of the session. A target of 0 is written on the 10:00:00 bar of the next session and filled at the 10:01:00 open, so the position spans the overnight gap plus the first 31 minutes. Between decision points the target is held; drift is only rebalanced when the position moves more than 2% of book. Everything outside the block is cash (no BIL leg).
rules: Regime: QQQ close (previous day) above its 165-day SMA by more than 2% -> ON; below by more than 2% -> OFF; inside the band the state persists.
If the regime is ON, buy TQQQ at the 15:59:00 open of the session's last 1-minute bar.
Sell TQQQ at the 10:01:00 open of the next session (captures the overnight gap plus the first 30 minutes).
Otherwise hold cash; no BIL sleeve while flat.
Long-only, 0% or 100% TQQQ; no shorting, no borrowing, no leverage beyond TQQQ's own 3x daily reset.
strategies.verdict: Beats TQQQ on CAGR and drawdown on both windows at 1 bp (49.23%/42.66% 10y, 28.89%/34.54% 5y), but fails the CAGR test at 3 bp and 5 bp, loses to the plain daily SMA baseline on 5y CAGR, and its level moves +/-5 pp across innocent parameter choices. The edge is real (78% of TQQQ's log return is earned overnight) but the implementation cost decides whether it pays.

provenance.idea: Essentially all of the U.S. equity premium is earned outside trading hours, so a leveraged ETF's exposure can be narrowed to the overnight block.
provenance.source: Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008) - Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours: Like Night and Day
provenance.evidence: Documents that from 1993 onward the entire equity premium of major U.S. indices accrues in the non-trading (close-to-open) period while intraday returns are roughly flat. This is the origin of the 'own TQQQ only overnight' rule; my own measurement on QQQ/TQQQ 1-minute bars reproduces the same split (78.4% of TQQQ log return overnight).

provenance.idea: Overnight and intraday returns behave like two separate assets with separate clienteles, so the overnight block can carry a persistent premium.
provenance.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) - A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns (JFE)
provenance.evidence: Models overnight and intraday returns as driven by different investor clienteles and shows the overnight-minus-intraday spread forecasts returns; supports treating the overnight block as a distinct, persistent exposure rather than noise. This is the PDF I actually read (DOI 10.1016/j.jfineco.2019.03.011).

provenance.idea: The first half hour of the session carries a large positive return and predicts the last half hour, so the exit should be after 10:00 rather than at 09:30.
provenance.source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018) - Market Intraday Momentum (JFE 129(2), 394-414)
provenance.evidence: Shows the first half-hour market return is large, positive and significantly predicts the last half-hour return on SPY, i.e. the opening half hour is an information-heavy, positively-drifting block. Supports extending the holding window from 09:31 to 10:01. My own measurement agrees on the sign (TQQQ 09:30->10:00 block +8.09% CAGR standalone) but shows the size is era-dependent.

provenance.idea: U.S. equity returns are large and positive during the opening hours of the U.S. session, tied to the overlap with European markets.
provenance.source: New York Fed Staff Report 917 - The Opening Hours of European Markets and U.S. Equity Returns
provenance.evidence: Documents economically large and statistically significant positive U.S. equity returns in the opening hours, which is the mechanism behind the positive first-30-minutes block the strategy captures by exiting at 10:01 instead of 09:31.

provenance.idea: Independent decomposition of SPY/QQQ returns into overnight and intraday legs confirms the direction of the overnight effect outside my own sample construction.
provenance.source: Tideline / JBP Capital - Overnight vs Intraday Returns: SPY and QQQ, 1999-2026
provenance.evidence: Reports that the overnight leg grew far more than the intraday leg for both SPY and QQQ over 1999-2026, with the QQQ intraday leg materially weaker. Used only as a cross-check on the sign of the effect; not used to set any parameter.

provenance.idea: The last 30 minutes of the session are negative for TQQQ in this sample, so the position should be flat into the close.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: Measured on local 1-minute TQQQ bars, 2,700 sessions: the 15:30->16:00 block has -5.74% CAGR standalone and -1.48 bp/day mean, with a 64% drawdown. This is a sample-specific finding, not taken from a paper.

provenance.idea: A 165-day SMA on QQQ with a 2% hysteresis band is a sufficient regime filter for a 3x long position.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source (165-day SMA taken from research/README.md daily baseline)
provenance.evidence: The 165-day SMA is the repository's reference baseline, not fitted here. The 2% hysteresis band is my addition and is the single largest fitted choice: it cuts regime switches from 41 to 11 in 10.7 years and is worth ~8 pp of CAGR. Band 1%, 2%, 3% and 5% all pass, so the sign is stable even though the magnitude is not.

provenance.idea: Benchmark and target to beat: TQQQ buy-and-hold on the same 1-minute bars and windows.
provenance.source: Repository benchmark (research/README.md and research/bt.py)
provenance.evidence: TQQQ 39.28% CAGR / 81.68% max DD over 10y and 13.47% / 81.68% over 5y; daily SMA baseline 45.31% / 58.71% and 34.61% / 36.86%. Re-measured on the 1-minute panel: TQQQ 39.38% / 82.29% and 14.29% / 82.29%.

rejectedSources.source: McConnell & Xu (2008) - Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month (Financial Analysts Journal 64(2))
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Tested as a 24h-hold overlay on the turn-of-month window (last 1 + first 3 trading days). It improved the backtest to 55.29%/34.25% 10y and 35.63%/31.60% 5y at 1 bp and cut fills from 4,069 to 3,293, but failed the stability screen: TOM day-sessions beat non-TOM in only 7 of 11 years, per-year t-stats on the difference are mostly below 2 (max 1.98), and the width sweep rises monotonically toward wider windows (49.2% at 0 days to 68.4% at 11 days), so the gain cannot be separated from simply holding more market beta in a bull decade. strategies.name: Gap capitulation
strategies.tagline: The cross-overnight capitulation bounce is real, but it is not incremental to the winner.
strategies.summary: In a QQQ 165-day bull regime, a QQQ close of -2% or worse is followed by a positive next-session TQQQ open-to-close (+0.92%, t=2.33, n=97), and a -3% intraday low by +1.21% (t=1.96, n=52); a 20-day drawdown of -10% or worse by +2.45% (t=2.19, n=24). The effect is concentrated in sessions where the regime is still on at the next open (+0.99%, t=2.44, n=88; +2.78%, t=2.26, n=19) and vanishes when the regime is off. But the round-1 winner is already long on those days and its 4% stop re-enters at the next open, so the event adds nothing; a standalone gap-down event strategy makes only 7.74%/21.22% (10y) and 7.95%/8.20% (5y) at 1 bp and fails versus TQQQ.
strategies.decision: The event is measured on the event day: a gap is known at the 09:30 open, a close/drawdown event at the 15:59 close. If the event day is in a bull regime (QQQ close > 165-day SMA using prior closes), buy TQQQ at the next session's 09:30 open (weights set on the last bar of the event day, filled at the next open). The standalone test holds one session and exits at the following open; the 4% stop is measured from the session open, uses the current minute close and fills at the next minute open, and the trade also exits on regime off. The same event is used as an overlay test on the winner, never as a look-ahead: no signal uses the event day's close to trade the event day itself.
rules: Bull regime: QQQ prior close > 165-day SMA of QQQ daily closes; otherwise BIL.
Standalone event tested: QQQ gap <= -1.5% at the event day's open, in a bull regime; buy TQQQ at the next session's open only if the regime is still on at the event day's close.
Hold 1 session and exit at the next open; 4% stop below the session open, next-minute fill; exit on regime off.
Event-study signals (next-open entry, 1/3/5-session holds): QQQ gap <= -1.5/-2/-3%; TQQQ gap <= -5/-6/-8%; QQQ intraday low <= -2/-3/-4%; QQQ close <= -2/-2.5%; QQQ 20-day drawdown <= -8/-10%.
Winner-overlay tests: arm the 4% stop on a gap-down (gap-arm), suppress the stop once QQQ <= -3% from the prior close, and arm the stop after a prior QQQ -2% day.
strategies.verdict: Clean negative. The cross-overnight bounce is statistically real (t about 2.0-2.4 for the close and intraday-low events) but redundant: the winner's 4% stop already exits the crash and re-enters at the next open. The standalone event strategy is not investable (7.74%/21.22% 10y, 7.95%/8.20% 5y at 1 bp; 6.02%/21.22% and 6.51%/8.53% at 10 bp) and loses to TQQQ by about 31 pp and 5.5 pp of CAGR. The best winner overlay (gap-arm) is 58.90%/44.56% 10y and 49.88%/33.49% 5y, statistically unchanged from the winner's 58.80%/44.56% and 49.88%/33.49%. Main caveat: the event samples are small (gap <= -3%: n=8; TQQQ gap <= -8%: n=8; 20-day DD <= -10%: n=24) and the whole family is a 2020/2022-heavy tail study.
