provenance.idea: Large one-day declines can reverse over the next session, but the effect is a liquidity/bid-ask phenomenon, not overreaction; long-horizon performance after large declines is poor.
provenance.source: Cox & Peterson (1994) - Stock Returns following Large One-Day Declines
provenance.evidence: Finds short-term reversals after large one-day declines and attributes them to bid-ask bounce and market liquidity; finds no evidence for the overreaction hypothesis and reports extended-horizon underperformance. Used as the skeptical prior and as the reason the standalone event edge was not assumed to be tradable.

provenance.idea: Overnight and intraday returns reverse across periods, and short-term reversal-strategy profits are earned overnight.
provenance.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019) - A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
provenance.evidence: Documents strong own-component continuation and an offsetting cross-period reversal; the short-term reversal strategy earns its profit overnight. This is the direct motivation for entering at the next session's open rather than intraday.

provenance.idea: The U.S. equity premium is earned mostly overnight.
provenance.source: Cliff, Cooper & Gulen (2008) - Return Differences between Trading and Non-Trading Hours: Like Night and Day
provenance.evidence: Decomposes the equity premium into open-to-close and close-to-open; the overnight leg carries essentially all of it for indices, futures and stocks. Supports the next-open entry as the natural place to capture a post-capitulation bounce.

provenance.idea: The overnight drift is large, persistent and visible across markets.
provenance.source: Haghani, Ragulin & Dewey (2022/2024) - Night Moves: Is the Overnight Drift the Grandmother of All Market Anomalies?
provenance.evidence: Documents the overnight drift and its persistence; used as background for why the cross-overnight version of the event is the one worth testing.

provenance.idea: Gap downs are slightly more likely to be reversed intraday than gap ups, but the edge is small.
provenance.source: QuantifiedStrategies - How Often Do Overnight Gaps Get Reversed?
provenance.evidence: SPY sample of 5,006 gaps: 52% of gap downs reversed intraday versus 35% of gap ups; GLD and TLT show no bias. Used to define the gap-down event, not as proof of a tradable next-session edge.

provenance.idea: A gap down does not reliably predict the day's direction; the open-to-close edge is near a coin flip.
provenance.source: QuantifiedStrategies - What's the Chance the Market Closes Lower After a Gap Down?
provenance.evidence: Reports a 53% chance the market closes above the open after a gap down and a 47% chance it closes lower. Consistent with the weak same-day gap-fade result and the decision to use the next session's open.

provenance.idea: Big gap downs have a small positive open-to-close drift and fill only about 40% of the time.
provenance.source: TradeIntel - SPX 0DTE: What an Opening Gap Tells You About the Day
provenance.evidence: 33 years of S&P 500 gaps: big gap down (>1%) open-to-close +0.11%, 52% green, 40% fill. Used as the external benchmark for the same-day gap behavior; my data shows the stronger bounce is in the first hour, not in the next session.

provenance.idea: A gap-down reversal may build over three sessions.
provenance.source: Mosaic Research - What Happens After the S&P 500 Gaps Down?
provenance.evidence: 10 matched US500 sessions, 8 of 10 higher after 3 days, median +103 points; the author explicitly warns that 10 observations cannot establish a stable probability. Used only as an anecdote; rejected as statistical evidence.

provenance.idea: After a 2% or 3% down day, the next session is up about 55-58% of the time with a small positive median.
provenance.source: jorgai - Buy the Dip: Every S&P 500 Dip Since 1950, Measured
provenance.evidence: S&P 500 since 1950: after a 2% down day, next day median +0.2%, 55% up; after 3%, +0.3%, 58% up; month-ahead +2.4% after 2% days. Used to sanity-check the magnitude of the cross-overnight bounce; my regime-on numbers are larger because of the bull-regime filter.

provenance.idea: Buying QQQ after a 2% fall and holding five days is not a reliable standalone edge after costs.
provenance.source: Finabase - Buying after large one-day falls: the rules and a backtest
provenance.evidence: QQQ daily sample: 16 of 28 next days up after a 2% fall, five-day outcomes ranging from +9.07% to -9.87%, about 82% cash, 10 bp round-trip costs. Its failure matches my standalone result and is why the event is reported as an overlay candidate, not a strategy.

provenance.idea: Stop-loss rules add value when returns have momentum/regime shifts; do not suppress a stop into a falling market.
provenance.source: Kaminski & Lo (2014) - When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses?
provenance.evidence: Shows stop-losses add value when returns have momentum and cost little when they do not. Used to motivate the stop-suppression test and to interpret the result: suppressing the stop once QQQ is -3% from the prior close is much worse (52.37%/56.89% 10y).

provenance.idea: Intraday and overnight returns can be decomposed, and end-of-day price pressure reverses overnight.
provenance.source: Bondarenko & Muravyev (2021) - Market Return Around the Clock: A Puzzle (NY Fed Staff Report 917)
provenance.evidence: Documents the intraday/overnight pattern and end-of-day price pressure. Consistent with the cross-overnight entry, though not specific to gap-down or capitulation events.

provenance.idea: Selling a QQQ gap down is harmful; after a QQQ gap below -2% in a regime-on market the next 60 minutes of TQQQ average +223 bp (t=3.61, n=20).
provenance.source: Local round-2 agent 17 report - overnight-crash-filter
provenance.evidence: Section 7.2 of the local report: gap-down exits cost 3-8 pp of CAGR and do not reduce drawdown; the first hour after a gap down bounces. I reproduced the same direction in my own data and therefore did not build a gap-fade strategy.

provenance.idea: The round-1 winner's stop-and-next-open re-entry already captures the post-capitulation bounce; after a -3% QQQ drawdown the next session open-to-close averages +1.17% (62% win, n=48).
provenance.source: Local round-1 report - intraday-mean-reversion
provenance.evidence: Event study of the 3% stop: overnight gap -0.69%, next session open-to-close +1.17%. This is the direct antecedent of my next-open entry and the reason the event overlay is redundant.

provenance.idea: The 165-day QQQ SMA regime and the armed 4% intraday stop are the round-1 winner.
provenance.source: Local round-1 report - daily-regime-minute-entry / this repo
provenance.evidence: The winner's exact rules and 58.80%/44.56% (10y) and 49.88%/33.49% (5y) at 1 bp. I reproduced these exactly, including 5 bp (54.60%/47.08%, 45.89%/34.13%) and 10 bp (49.50%/50.06%, 41.05%/34.93%).

provenance.idea: All event definitions, threshold choices, overlay tests and the standalone metrics in result.json.
provenance.source: Own test / no external source
provenance.evidence: research/agents2/gap-capitulation-reversal/result.json and strategy.py: 160 winner stop events, the event-study grid, gap-arm at 1.5%, stop suppression at 3%, prior-day-down arm at 2%, and the standalone QQQ gap <= -1.5%/1-day/4%-stop run at 1/5/10 bp.

rejectedSources.source: QuantifiedStrategies - Gap Reversal (the page currently cited by the web export)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The page could not be retrieved (bot verification), so it cannot be cited as the exact source of the rule. More importantly, the gap-fade premise was tested and rejected as a standalone: the gap-down bounce is concentrated in the first hour and the next-session edge is weak (QQQ gap <= -2%: +1.10%, t=0.86, n=20), and the standalone strategy is far below TQQQ.

rejectedSources.source: Mosaic Research - What Happens After the S&P 500 Gaps Down?
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Only 10 observations and one April 2025 tariff-shock outlier; the author warns it is not a stable probability. Used only as an anecdote, not as evidence for a rule.

rejectedSources.source: Finabase - Buying after large one-day falls (QQQ, 2% fall, 5-day hold)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: The rule is not a standalone edge after costs in the source's own test (16/28 next days up, wide +9%/-10% spread, 82% cash), and my standalone QQQ gap event fails the same way. Kept only as a caution about buying the first bounce.

rejectedSources.source: Own idea - buy the gap open and fade the gap down
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Tested and rejected: the event-day open-to-close return after a QQQ close <= -2% is -5.96% (the down day continues), and the gap-down bounce is in the first hour (+2.09% for gap <= -2% and low <= -3%, t=2.47), not in the next session. A next-open entry is the only causal version of the trade.

rejectedSources.source: Own idea - suppress the 4% stop once QQQ is -3% from the prior close (do not stop into capitulation)
rejectedSources.why_rejected: Tested and much worse: 52.37%/56.89% (10y) and 45.43%/39.29% (5y) versus the winner's 58.80%/44.56% and 49.88%/33.49%. The stop is the crash hedge; removing it at the moment of maximum stress destroys the result.

corrections: The web page conflates the event study with the standalone strategy. The metrics 7.74%/21.22% (10y) and 7.95%/8.20% (5y) belong to the QQQ gap <= -1.5%, 1-day, 4%-stop standalone, not to the 'QQQ close <= -2% or -3% intraday low' signal. Either state the gap <= -1.5% entry and the 4% stop explicitly, or relabel the metrics as the gap-down variant.

Add the exact 5 bp standalone metrics: 6.97%/21.22% (10y) and 7.31%/8.34% (5y). The 10 bp values are 6.02%/21.22% and 6.51%/8.53%. The page currently shows only 1 bp, which makes the result look better than the honest cost range; the pass/fail is unchanged because the CAGR is 31 pp below TQQQ.

Do not imply that the gap-arm overlay improves the winner. Winner + gap-arm 1.5% is 58.90%/44.56% (10y) and 49.88%/33.49% (5y), versus the winner's 58.80%/44.56% and 49.88%/33.49%; the +0.10 pp is one extra fill, not an edge. The MA20 gate already arms the stop on the large gap-down days.

Do not promote the prior-day-down arm. Its +2.26 pp 10y CAGR (61.06%/44.56%) comes from exactly two sessions, 2020-06-12 and 2020-09-04; the 5y result is identical to the winner. It is a two-event artifact and should not be presented as an overlay.

The stop-event claim in the report must be causal. Split by the QQQ drawdown at the time of the stop, the <= -3% bucket is n=5 and -0.93% per event (t=-0.40), while the > -3% bucket is n=155 and +0.46% (t=1.81); overall stop-vs-hold is +0.41% per event (t=1.63). The earlier +2.69% (t=3.38) figure conditioned on the day's eventual low, which is ex-post and should not be quoted as a causal stop-quality result.

Attach the 't about 2.0-2.4' claim to the close/intraday-low events, not the gap events. QQQ close <= -2%: +0.92%, t=2.33, n=97; QQQ low <= -3%: +1.21%, t=1.96, n=52; regime-on subsets: +0.99%, t=2.44, n=88 and +1.33%, t=2.10, n=46. The gap signals are weaker: QQQ gap <= -2% +1.10%, t=0.86, n=20; TQQQ gap <= -5% +0.99%, t=1.06, n=34; QQQ gap <= -3% n=8.

Do not cite the standalone's low drawdown as a risk-management success without the exposure caveat. It beats TQQQ CAGR in 8/28 ten-year rolling windows and 13/20 five-year windows, with lower drawdown in 28/28 and 20/20 only because it is in TQQQ about 5% of the time. The winner beats TQQQ CAGR in 23/28 and 19/20.

The source attribution in the web export (GAP_STRATEGY, LOU, CLIFF) is directionally right but too loose. GAP_STRATEGY (QuantifiedStrategies Gap Reversal) could not be retrieved and was not the exact source used; the gap evidence I actually used is the QuantifiedStrategies gap-down frequency pages and the TradeIntel 33-year gap table. Lou-Polk-Skouras and Cliff-Cooper-Gulen support the overnight entry, not the gap-down event itself. The 165-day SMA regime and the 4% stop are repo/round-1 constructs, not from a paper.

The page should say explicitly that this family is an event study, not a strategy: the strongest signal (QQQ 20-day drawdown <= -10%) has n=24 and is concentrated in 2020 and 2022, and the gap <= -3% signal has n=8. The small-sample caveat is material.
